sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十三】起昭陽大淵獻，盡閼逢困敦七月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 63] Beginning from Zhaoyang Dayuanxian, ending in the seventh month of Yanfeng Kundun; in all a little more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 63] From the year guihai (843) through the seventh month of the year jiazi (844)—a little over one year in all.

sentences.zh: 武宗至道昭肅孝皇帝中會昌三年（

translations.literal: In the third year of Huichang of Emperor Wuzong, the Filial Emperor of Supreme Way, Solemn Clarity (
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huichang of Emperor Wuzong (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元八四三年）

translations.literal: guihai, corresponding to 843 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guihai, 843 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，回鶻烏介可汗帥眾侵逼振武，劉沔遣麟州刺史石雄、都知兵馬使王逢帥沙陀朱邪赤心三部及契苾、拓跋三千騎襲其牙帳，沔自以大軍繼之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Uyghur Khan Wujie led his forces to press upon Zhenwu. Liu Mian dispatched Linzhou Prefect Shi Xiong and Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Feng to lead three divisions of the Shatuo Zhuye Chixin together with three thousand horsemen of the Qibi and Tuoba to raid his royal encampment; Mian himself followed with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Uyghur khan Wujie led his forces against Zhenwu. Liu Mian sent Linzhou prefect Shi Xiong and military commissioner Wang Feng at the head of three Shatuo Zhuye Chixin divisions plus three thousand Qibi and Tuoba cavalry to strike the khan's encampment, while Mian followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 雄至振武，登城望回鶻之眾寡，見氈車數十乘，從者皆衣朱碧，類華人。

translations.literal: When Xiong reached Zhenwu, he mounted the wall to observe the size of the Uyghur force and saw several dozen felt-wheeled carts; the attendants all wore red and green garments resembling those of Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xiong reached Zhenwu, he climbed the wall to gauge the Uyghur strength and saw several dozen felt-wheeled carts; the attendants all wore red and green in a style that looked Chinese.

sentences.zh: 使諜問之，曰：「公主帳也。」

translations.literal: He sent a spy to inquire and was told: "It is the princess's tent."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a spy to ask and was told, "That is the princess's tent."

sentences.zh: 雄使諜告之曰：「公主至此，家也，當求歸路！

translations.literal: Xiong had the spy tell her: "Princess, you have come to your homeland and ought to seek the road home!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong had the spy tell her, "Princess, you have reached home—now you should find your way back!

sentences.zh: 今將出兵擊可汗，請公主潛與侍從相保，駐車勿動！」

translations.literal: We are about to send troops to attack the khan; I ask the princess to keep quietly with her attendants, halt the carts, and not move!"
translations.idiomatic: We are about to attack the khan. Please stay quietly with your attendants, keep your carts where they are, and do not move!"

sentences.zh: 雄乃鑿城為十餘穴，引兵夜出，直攻可汗牙帳。

translations.literal: Xiong then cut more than ten breaches in the wall, led his troops out by night, and struck straight at the khan's encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong then broke more than ten holes through the wall, led his men out by night, and drove straight at the khan's encampment.

sentences.zh: 至其帳下，虜乃覺之。

translations.literal: When they reached the tents, the barbarians only then became aware of them.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they reached the encampment did the enemy realize what was happening.

sentences.zh: 可汗大驚，不知所為，棄輜重走，雄追擊之。

translations.literal: The khan was greatly alarmed and did not know what to do; he abandoned his baggage train and fled, and Xiong pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: The khan was thrown into panic and fled, abandoning his baggage train; Shi Xiong gave chase.

sentences.zh: 庚子，大破回鶻於殺胡山，可汗被瘡，與數百騎遁去，雄迎太和公主以歸。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he inflicted a great defeat on the Uyghurs at Mount Shahu; the khan was wounded and escaped with several hundred horsemen, and Xiong welcomed Princess Taihe back.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi he routed the Uyghurs at Mount Shahu. The khan was wounded and fled with a few hundred riders, and Shi Xiong escorted Princess Taihe home.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬級，降其部落二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Ten thousand heads were cut off, and more than twenty thousand of their tribesmen surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand heads were taken, and more than twenty thousand tribesmen submitted.

sentences.zh: 丙午，劉沔捷奏至。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Liu Mian's report of victory arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu, Liu Mian's victory report reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 李思忠入朝，自以回鶻降將，懼邊將猜忌，乞並弟思貞等及愛弘順皆歸闕庭。

translations.literal: Li Sizhong came to court; considering himself a Uyghur defector, he feared suspicion from frontier generals and requested that his younger brother Sizhen and others, together with Ai Hongshun, all return to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhong came to court. As a former Uyghur defector, he feared the distrust of frontier commanders and asked that his brother Sizhen and the others, along with Ai Hongshun, all be brought back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以石雄為豐州都防禦使。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Shi Xiong was appointed Defender-in-Chief of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, Shi Xiong was made Defender-in-Chief of Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 烏介可汗走保黑車子族，其潰兵多詣幽州降。

translations.literal: Khan Wujie fled to take refuge with the Heichezi tribe; many of his scattered troops went to Youzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Wujie fled for protection to the Heichezi tribe, while many of his broken troops surrendered at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengshen, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day (gengshen), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔停歸義軍，以其士卒分隸諸道為騎兵，優給糧賜。

translations.literal: An edict dissolved the Army of Returning Allegiance and distributed its soldiers among the various circuits as cavalry, with generous provisions and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict disbanded the Army of Returning Allegiance and assigned its soldiers as cavalry to the various circuits, with generous rations and rewards.

sentences.zh: 辛未，黠戛斯遣使者注吾合索獻名馬二，詔太僕卿趙蕃飲勞之。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Kirghiz sent the envoy Zhunwu Hesuo to present two fine horses; the emperor ordered Grand Master of the Stud Zhao Fan to feast and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, the Kirghiz sent the envoy Zhunwu Hesuo with two fine horses as tribute, and the emperor ordered Grand Master of the Stud Zhao Fan to entertain and reward him.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，上引對，班在勃海使之上。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the emperor summoned him for audience, placing his rank above the Bohai envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, the emperor received him in audience and ranked him above the Bohai envoy.

sentences.zh: 上欲令趙蕃就頡戛斯求安西、北庭，李德裕等上言：「安西去京師七千餘里，北庭五千餘里，借使得之，當復置都護，以唐兵萬人戍之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to send Zhao Fan to the Kirghiz to request Anxi and Beiting. Li Deyu and others submitted: "Anxi is more than seven thousand li from the capital and Beiting more than five thousand li; even if we obtained them by borrowing another's strength, we would have to reestablish protectorates and garrison them with ten thousand Tang troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted Zhao Fan to ask the Kirghiz to return Anxi and Beiting. Li Deyu and others argued, "Anxi lies more than seven thousand li from the capital and Beiting more than five thousand. Even if we recovered them, we would have to restore the protectorates and station ten thousand Tang troops there.

sentences.zh: 不知此兵於何處追發，饋運從何道得通，此乃用實費以易虛名，非計也。」

translations.literal: It is not known from where these troops could be raised, or by what route supplies could reach them. This would be exchanging real expense for an empty name—it is no plan at all."
translations.idiomatic: No one knows where those troops would come from or how supplies could reach them. That would mean spending real resources for an empty title—not a sound policy."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事崔珙罷為右僕射。

translations.literal: Cui Gong, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal to the Department of State Affairs, was removed and made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, was dismissed and made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯求冊命，李德裕奏，宜與之結歡，令自將兵求殺使者罪人，及討黑車子。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz requested investiture. Li Deyu submitted that Tang should win their friendship and have them lead troops themselves to seek the criminals who had killed the envoy and to campaign against the Heichezi.
translations.idiomatic: The Kirghiz asked to be formally invested. Li Deyu argued that Tang should win them over and have them lead their own troops to punish those who had killed the envoy and to attack the Heichezi.

sentences.zh: 上恐加可汗之名即不修臣禮，踵回鶻故事求歲遺及賣馬，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: The emperor feared that granting the title of khan would mean they would not observe the rituals of a subject state and would follow the Uyghur precedent in demanding annual gifts and horse sales; he hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried that once granted the title of khan, they would refuse proper subject protocol and follow the Uyghur example by demanding annual gifts and horse-trade privileges. He hesitated, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏：「黠戛斯已自稱可汗，今欲藉其力，恐不可吝此名。

translations.literal: Deyu submitted: "The Kirghiz already call themselves khan; now that we wish to borrow their strength, I fear we cannot begrudge this title.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu argued, "The Kirghiz already style themselves khan. If we mean to use their strength, we can hardly be stingy with the title.

sentences.zh: 回鶻有平安、史之功，故歲賜絹二萬匹，且與之和市。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs had the merit of suppressing the An and Shi rebellions, and so received an annual gift of twenty thousand bolts of silk and were allowed peaceful trade.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs had helped put down the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellions, which is why they received twenty thousand bolts of silk each year and were allowed to trade peacefully.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯未嘗有功於中國，豈敢遽求賂遺乎！

translations.literal: The Kirghiz have never rendered service to China—how would they dare suddenly to demand bribes and gifts!
translations.idiomatic: The Kirghiz have never done China any service—how would they dare demand gifts so soon!

sentences.zh: 若慮其不臣，當與之約，必如回鶻稱臣，乃行冊命；

translations.literal: If we worry that they will not be subject, we should stipulate with them that investiture will be carried out only after they submit as subjects, like the Uyghurs;
translations.idiomatic: If we fear they will not submit, we should require them to declare themselves subjects as the Uyghurs did before granting investiture;

sentences.zh: 又當敘同姓以親之，使執子孫之禮。」

translations.literal: we should also recount shared surname to draw them close and have them observe the rites due from descendants."
translations.idiomatic: and we should claim kinship through a shared surname so that they observe the rites owed by descendants."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，太和公主至京師，改封安定大長公主，詔宰相帥百官迎謁於章敬寺前。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Princess Taihe reached the capital; her title was changed to Grand Princess of Anding, and an edict ordered the chief ministers to lead the officials in greeting her before Zhangjing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin, Princess Taihe reached the capital. She was re-titled Grand Princess of Anding, and the chief ministers were ordered to lead the officials in welcoming her before Zhangjing Temple.

sentences.zh: 公主詣光順門，去盛服，脫簪珥，謝回鶻負恩、和親無狀之罪。

translations.literal: The princess went to Guangshun Gate, put off her splendid garments, removed her hairpins and earrings, and apologized for the Uyghurs' ingratitude and the disgrace of the marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangshun Gate the princess put aside her finery, removed her hairpins and earrings, and apologized for the Uyghurs' ingratitude and the shame brought upon the marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使慰諭，然後入宮。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to comfort and instruct her, after which she entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to comfort her, and only then did she enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 陽安等六公主不來慰問安定公主，各罰俸物及封絹。

translations.literal: The six princesses, including Yang'an, did not come to console Princess Anding; each was fined salary goods and silk from her fief.
translations.idiomatic: The six princesses, including Yang'an, failed to visit Princess Anding; each was fined salary goods and fief silk.

sentences.zh: 賜魏博節度使何重順名弘敬。

translations.literal: He Chongshun, military commissioner of Weibo, was granted the name Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He Chongshun, military commissioner of Weibo, was granted the personal name Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 三月，以太僕卿趙蕃為安撫黠戛斯使。

translations.literal: In the third month, Grand Master of the Stud Zhao Fan was made envoy to pacify the Kirghiz.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Grand Master of the Stud Zhao Fan was appointed envoy to the Kirghiz.

sentences.zh: 上命李德草《賜黠戛斯可汗書》，諭以「貞觀二十一年，黠戛斯先君身自入朝，授左屯衛將軍、堅昆都督，迄於天寶，朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Li De to draft "A Letter Bestowed upon the Kirghiz Khan," instructing him that "In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, the Kirghiz forebear came in person to court and was appointed General of the Left Garrison Guard and Commander of Jiankun; down to the Tianbao era, tribute never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li De to draft a letter to the Kirghiz khan explaining that "in the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, your forebear came to court in person and was appointed General of the Left Garrison Guard and Commander of Jiankun; tribute continued without break down to the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 比為回鶻所隔，回鶻凌虐諸蕃，可汗能復仇雪怨，茂功壯節，近古無儔。

translations.literal: Lately, cut off by the Uyghurs, while the Uyghurs oppressed the various tribes, the khan was able to avenge wrongs and wipe away grievances—a splendid achievement and heroic integrity unmatched in recent ages.
translations.idiomatic: More recently you were cut off by the Uyghurs while they bullied the frontier peoples. That you could avenge those wrongs is a splendid achievement unmatched in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 今回鶻殘兵不滿千人，散投山谷，可汗既與為怨，須盡殲夷。

translations.literal: Now the Uyghur remnant forces number fewer than a thousand, scattered into valleys; since the khan already bears enmity toward them, they must be utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur remnants now number fewer than a thousand, scattered in the valleys. Since you already bear a grudge against them, you must wipe them out completely.

sentences.zh: 倘留餘燼，必生後患。

translations.literal: If any embers are left, later troubles will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: Leave any embers alive and trouble will follow.

sentences.zh: 又聞可汗受氏之原，與我同族，國家承北平太守之後，可汗乃都尉苗裔。

translations.literal: It is also heard that the origin of the khan's surname is the same clan as ours: the state inherits from the Later Administrator of Beiping, while the khan is descended from a commandant.
translations.idiomatic: We also hear that your clan name shares our ancestry: the Tang house descends from the Administrator of Beiping, while you descend from a commandant of old.

sentences.zh: 以此合族，尊卑可知。

translations.literal: By this shared clan, senior and junior rank may be known.
translations.idiomatic: By this kinship, the proper order of senior and junior is clear.

sentences.zh: 今欲冊命可汗，特加美號，緣未知可汗意，且遣諭懷。

translations.literal: We now wish to invest the khan and specially add a fine title; because we do not yet know the khan's mind, we first send this message to convey our goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: We now wish to invest you and bestow a fine title. Not yet knowing your wishes, we send this letter first to explain our intent.

sentences.zh: 待趙蕃回日，別命使展禮。」

translations.literal: When Zhao Fan returns, a separate envoy will be appointed to perform the full rites."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Fan returns, we will send another envoy to perform the full ceremony."

sentences.zh: 自回鶻至塞上及黠戛斯入貢，每有詔敕，上多命德裕草之。

translations.literal: From the time the Uyghurs reached the frontier and the Kirghiz sent tribute, whenever there were edicts and orders, the emperor mostly had Deyu draft them.
translations.idiomatic: From the Uyghur crisis on the frontier through the Kirghiz tribute missions, the emperor usually had Li Deyu draft the edicts.

sentences.zh: 德裕請委翰林學士，上曰：「學士不能盡人意，須卿自為之。」

translations.literal: Deyu requested that the matter be entrusted to the Hanlin academicians. The emperor said: "The academicians cannot fully express my intent; you must do it yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu asked to leave the drafting to the Hanlin academicians. The emperor replied, "The academicians cannot capture what I mean—you must write it yourself."

sentences.zh: 劉沔奏：「歸義軍回鶻三千餘人及酋長四十三人准詔分隸諸道，皆大呼，連營據滹沱河，不肯從命，已盡誅之。

translations.literal: Liu Mian submitted: "More than three thousand Uyghurs of the Army of Returning Allegiance and forty-three chieftains, pursuant to the edict assigning them to the various circuits, all shouted in protest, joined camps, and occupied the Hutuo River, refusing to obey orders; they have all been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian reported, "More than three thousand Uyghurs of the Army of Returning Allegiance and forty-three chieftains, ordered by edict to be distributed among the circuits, shouted in protest, camped together on the Hutuo River, and refused to obey. They have all been executed.

sentences.zh: 回鶻降幽州者前後三萬餘人，皆散錄諸道。」

translations.literal: Uyghurs who surrendered at Youzhou numbered more than thirty thousand in all and were all dispersed and registered among the circuits."
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty thousand Uyghurs who had surrendered at Youzhou were distributed and registered among the circuits."

sentences.zh: 李德裕追論維州悉怛謀事云：「維州據高山絕頂，三面臨江，在戎虜平川之沖，是漢地入兵之路。

translations.literal: Li Deyu revisited the affair of Weizhou and Shedianmo, saying: "Weizhou stands on a high mountain peak with rivers on three sides; it lies at the crossing of the barbarians' flat lands and is the route by which Han territory receives troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu reopened the case of Weizhou and Shedianmo, arguing, "Weizhou sits on a high peak with rivers on three sides. It commands the barbarians' open country and is the gateway by which troops enter Han territory.

sentences.zh: 初，河、隴並沒，唯此獨存。

translations.literal: At first, the He and Long regions were both lost, and this alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the He and Long regions had both fallen, this was the only place left.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃潛以婦人嫁此州門者，二十年後，兩男長成，竊開壘門，引兵夜入，遂為所陷，號曰無憂城。

translations.literal: The Tibetans secretly married women to men at the gates of this prefecture; twenty years later, when the two sons had grown, they secretly opened the fortress gate by night and led troops in, and the place was thereby lost—it was called the City Without Worry.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans secretly married women to men at the prefecture gates. Twenty years later, when the two sons had grown up, they opened the gate by night and let Tibetan troops in. The city fell and was renamed the City Without Worry.

sentences.zh: 從此得並力於西邊，更無虞於南路。

translations.literal: From this they were able to combine their strength on the western frontier and had no further worry about the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they could concentrate their forces in the west and no longer feared attack from the south.

sentences.zh: 憑陵近甸，旰食累朝。

translations.literal: They pressed upon the nearby capital districts, and for successive reigns the rulers ate late in worry.
translations.idiomatic: They threatened the capital region itself, and for reign after reign the court ate late meals in alarm.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，韋皋欲經略河、湟，須此城為始。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, Wei Gao wished to recover the He and Huang regions and needed this city as the starting point.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era, Wei Gao planned to recover the He and Huang regions and needed this city as his first objective.

sentences.zh: 萬旅盡銳，急攻數年，雖擒論莽熱而還，城堅卒不可克。

translations.literal: Ten thousand troops with all their keenest strength attacked urgently for several years; although they captured Lun Mangre and returned, the city was strong and in the end could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand troops attacked at full strength for years. Though they captured Lun Mangre and withdrew, the city was too strong to be taken.

sentences.zh: 臣初到西蜀，外揚國威，中緝邊備。

translations.literal: When I first arrived in western Shu, outwardly I displayed the state's majesty and inwardly I put the frontier defenses in order.
translations.idiomatic: When I first arrived in western Shu, I displayed the empire's power abroad while tightening frontier defenses at home.

sentences.zh: 其維州熟臣信令，空壁來歸。

translations.literal: Weizhou, trusting my orders, came over with empty walls.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou, trusting my authority, surrendered with its defenses emptied.

sentences.zh: 臣始受其降，南蠻震懾，山西八國，皆願內屬。

translations.literal: When I first accepted their surrender, the southern barbarians were awed, and the eight states west of the mountains all wished to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When I first accepted their surrender, the southern tribes were awed, and the eight states west of the mountains all wished to submit.

sentences.zh: 其吐蕃合水、棲雞等城，既失險厄，自須抽歸，可減八處鎮兵，坐收千餘里舊地。

translations.literal: The Tibetan cities of Heshui, Qiji, and others, having lost their strategic passes, would naturally have to withdraw; eight garrisons could be reduced and more than a thousand li of old territory recovered without effort.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan strongholds such as Heshui and Qiji, once deprived of their passes, would have to pull back. Eight garrisons could be reduced and more than a thousand li of old territory recovered without a fight.

sentences.zh: 且維州未降前一年，吐蕃猶圍魯州，豈顧盟約！

translations.literal: Moreover, in the year before Weizhou surrendered, the Tibetans still besieged Luzhou—did they care about treaties!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the year before Weizhou surrendered, the Tibetans were still besieging Luzhou—what did they care for treaties!

sentences.zh: 臣受降之初，指天為誓，面許奏聞，各加酬賞。

translations.literal: When I first accepted the surrender, I swore by Heaven and promised in person to report it and grant rewards to each man.
translations.idiomatic: When I first accepted the surrender, I swore by Heaven and promised on the spot to report it and reward every man.

sentences.zh: 當時不與臣者，望風疾臣，詔臣執送悉怛謀等令彼自戮，臣寧忍以三百餘人命棄信偷安！

translations.literal: Those who opposed me at the time slandered me at every turn and ordered me to seize Shedianmo and the others and send them back to be executed by the enemy. How could I bear to abandon faith and seek my own ease at the cost of more than three hundred lives!
translations.idiomatic: My opponents slandered me at every turn and ordered me to seize Shedianmo and the others and send them back for execution. I could not abandon my word and seek my own comfort at the cost of more than three hundred lives!

sentences.zh: 累表陳論，乞垂矜捨，答詔嚴切，竟令執還。

translations.literal: I submitted memorial after memorial pleading for mercy, but the reply edict was stern, and in the end I was ordered to seize them and send them back.
translations.idiomatic: I memorialized again and again begging for mercy, but the reply was stern, and in the end I was ordered to seize them and send them back.

sentences.zh: 體備三木，輿於竹畚，及將就路，冤叫嗚嗚，將吏對臣，無不隕涕。

translations.literal: Their bodies fitted with the three wooden punishments, carried in bamboo baskets—when they were about to set out on the road, they cried out in injustice with wailing sounds; the officers facing me all shed tears without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Fitted with the three wooden punishments and carried in bamboo baskets, they wailed in protest as they were led away. Every officer who faced me wept.

sentences.zh: 其部送者更為蕃帥譏誚，雲既已降彼，何須送來！

translations.literal: The escort was further mocked by the Tibetan commander, who said: "Since they have already surrendered to you, why send them back!"
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan commander mocked the escort, saying, "If they have already surrendered to you, why send them back!"

sentences.zh: 復以此降人戮於漢境之上，恣行殘忍，用固攜離，至乃擲其嬰孩，承以槍槊。

translations.literal: Then these surrendered men were slaughtered on Han territory in wanton cruelty to cement alienation; they even tossed up their infants and caught them on spears.
translations.idiomatic: Then those who had surrendered were slaughtered on Han soil in wanton cruelty to drive a wedge between us, even tossing infants into the air and catching them on spears.

sentences.zh: 絕忠款之路，快凶虐之情，從古已來，未有此事。

translations.literal: The road of loyal submission was cut off and savage cruelty was gratified—since antiquity there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: The path of loyal submission was closed and savage cruelty was indulged—nothing like it had ever happened before.

sentences.zh: 雖時更一紀，而運屬千年，乞追獎忠魂，各加褒贈！」

translations.literal: Although more than a dozen years have passed, fate belongs to a thousand years—I beg that loyal souls be posthumously rewarded and each granted honors!"
translations.idiomatic: Though more than a dozen years have passed, their loyalty deserves to be remembered for a thousand years. I beg that these loyal souls be posthumously honored!"

sentences.zh: 詔贈悉怛謀右衛將軍。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded Shedianmo the title General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously awarded Shedianmo the title General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「論者多疑維州之取捨，不能決牛、李之是非。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: "Commentators mostly doubt the decision over Weizhou and cannot settle the rights and wrongs of the Niu and Li factions.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: "Commentators are divided over the Weizhou decision and cannot settle the rights and wrongs of the Niu and Li factions.

sentences.zh: 臣以為昔荀吳圍鼓，鼓人或請以城叛，吳弗許，曰：「或以吾城叛，吾所甚惡也，人以城來，吾獨何好焉！

translations.literal: I consider that in antiquity Xun Wu besieged Gu; someone in Gu asked to betray the city, and Wu would not allow it, saying: "If someone were to betray my city, that is what I most detest—when someone brings a city to me, why should I alone delight in it!
translations.idiomatic: I believe the old case of Xun Wu's siege of Gu settles the matter. When someone in Gu offered to betray the city, Wu refused, saying, "If someone betrayed my city, I would hate it—why should I delight when someone brings a city to me!

sentences.zh: 吾不可以欲城而邇奸。」

translations.literal: I cannot, because I desire the city, draw close to treachery."
translations.idiomatic: I must not court treachery just because I want the city."

sentences.zh: 使鼓人殺叛者而繕守備。

translations.literal: He had the people of Gu kill the traitor and repair the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He had the people of Gu execute the traitor and repair their defenses.

sentences.zh: 是時唐新與吐蕃修好而納其維州，以利言之，則維州大而信大；

translations.literal: At that time Tang had newly made peace with Tibet and yet accepted Weizhou from them; speaking of profit, both Weizhou and faith were great;
translations.idiomatic: Tang had just made peace with Tibet and then accepted Weizhou from them. Measured by gain, both Weizhou and good faith were great prizes;

sentences.zh: 以害言之，則維州緩而關中急。

translations.literal: speaking of harm, Weizhou was remote while Guanzhong was urgent.
translations.idiomatic: measured by harm, Weizhou was distant while the Guanzhong heartland was urgent.

sentences.zh: 然則為唐計者，宜何先乎？

translations.literal: Then for Tang's planning, which should come first?
translations.idiomatic: For Tang's interests, which should have come first?

sentences.zh: 悉怛謀在唐則為向化，在吐蕃不免為叛臣，其受誅也又何矜焉！

translations.literal: Shedianmo, in Tang, was one turning toward civilization; in Tibet he could not but be a rebel minister—why pity his execution!
translations.idiomatic: Shedianmo was a defector to Tang and a traitor to Tibet—why pity his execution!

sentences.zh: 且德裕所言者利也，僧孺所言者義也，匹夫徇利而亡義猶恥之，況天子乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, what Deyu spoke of was profit, and what Sengru spoke of was righteousness; even a common man who pursues profit and abandons righteousness is ashamed—how much more a Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu spoke of profit; Niu Sengru spoke of righteousness. Even a common man is ashamed to pursue profit at the cost of righteousness—how much more an emperor!

sentences.zh: 譬如鄰人有牛，逸而入於家，或勸其兄歸之，或勸其弟攘之。

translations.literal: It is like a neighbor's ox that strayed into one's house: one person advised the elder brother to return it, another advised the younger brother to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a neighbor's ox that strayed into one's yard: one brother was urged to return it, the other to keep it.

sentences.zh: 勸歸者曰：「攘之不義也，且致訟。」

translations.literal: The one who urged return said: "Seizing it is unrighteous, and will moreover lead to litigation."
translations.idiomatic: The one who urged return said, "Keeping it is wrong, and will only bring a lawsuit."

sentences.zh: 勸攘者曰：「彼嘗攘吾羊矣，何義之拘！

translations.literal: The one who urged seizure said: "They once seized our sheep—why be bound by righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: The one who urged keeping it said, "They stole our sheep once—why worry about righteousness now!

sentences.zh: 牛大畜也，鬻之可以富家。」

translations.literal: An ox is a large beast; selling it can enrich the household."
translations.idiomatic: An ox is valuable livestock—sell it and the household grows rich."

sentences.zh: 以是觀之，牛、李之是非，端可見矣。

translations.literal: Viewed in this way, the rights and wrongs of the Niu and Li factions can clearly be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, the rights and wrongs of the Niu and Li factions are plain enough.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛未，李德裕乞退就閒局。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinwei, Li Deyu requested to retire to an idle post.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinwei, Li Deyu asked to step down to an inactive post.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿每辭位，使我旬日不得聽。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Each time you resign your office, you keep me from holding audience for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Every time you resign, you keep me from holding court for ten days.

sentences.zh: 今大事皆未就，卿豈得求去！」

translations.literal: Now great affairs are all unfinished—how can you seek to leave!"
translations.idiomatic: Great affairs are still unfinished—how can you ask to leave now!"

sentences.zh: 初，昭義節度使劉從諫累表言仇士良罪惡，士良亦言從諫窺伺朝廷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Congjian, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, repeatedly memorialized about Qiu Shiliang's crimes; Shiliang also said Congjian was watching and probing the court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Congjian, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, had repeatedly memorialized against the eunuch Qiu Shiliang's crimes, while Shiliang in turn accused Congjian of watching the court for weakness.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，從諫有馬高九尺，獻之，上不受。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Congjian had a horse nine chi tall and presented it; the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Congjian offered him a horse nine chi tall, but the emperor refused it.

sentences.zh: 從諫以為士良所為，怒殺其馬，由是與朝廷相猜恨。

translations.literal: Congjian believed this was Shiliang's doing, angrily killed the horse, and from this mutual suspicion and resentment arose between him and the court.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian blamed Shiliang, killed the horse in anger, and from that point mutual suspicion and resentment grew between him and the court.

sentences.zh: 遂招納亡命，繕完兵械，鄰境皆潛為之備。

translations.literal: He then recruited fugitives, repaired weapons and armor, and neighboring territories all secretly made preparations against him.
translations.idiomatic: He began recruiting fugitives, rebuilding his arsenal, and neighboring territories quietly prepared against him.

sentences.zh: 從諫榷馬牧及商旅，歲入錢五萬緡，又賣鐵、煮鹽亦數萬緡。

translations.literal: Congjian monopolized horse pastures and merchant travel, taking in fifty thousand strings of cash per year; selling iron and boiling salt also brought in tens of thousands of strings.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian taxed horse pastures and merchant traffic for fifty thousand strings of cash a year, and iron sales and salt boiling brought in tens of thousands more.

sentences.zh: 大商皆假以牙職，使通好諸道，因為販易。

translations.literal: Great merchants were all given broker posts, sent to maintain friendly relations with the various circuits, and thereby conduct trade.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed major merchants as brokers to maintain ties with other circuits and conduct trade on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 商人倚從諫勢，所至多陵轢將吏，諸道皆惡之。

translations.literal: Merchants relied on Congjian's power; wherever they went they often bullied generals and officials, and all circuits hated them.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants traded on Congjian's power, bullying local officers wherever they went, and every circuit resented them.

sentences.zh: 從諫疾病，謂妻裴氏曰：「吾以忠直事朝廷，而朝廷不明我志，諸道皆不我與。

translations.literal: Congjian fell ill and said to his wife Lady Pei: "I have served the court with loyalty and integrity, yet the court does not understand my intent, and none of the circuits support me.
translations.idiomatic: When Congjian fell ill, he told his wife Lady Pei, "I have served the court loyally and uprightly, yet the court does not understand me, and none of the circuits stand with me.

sentences.zh: 我死，它人主此軍，則吾家無炊火矣！」

translations.literal: When I die, if another man commands this army, then there will be no cooking fire in our household!"
translations.idiomatic: When I die and another man takes this army, our household will have no fire in the hearth!"

sentences.zh: 乃與幕客張谷、陳揚庭謀效河北諸鎮，以弟右驍衛將軍從素之子稹為牙內都知兵馬使，從子匡周為中軍兵馬使，孔目官王協為押牙親事兵馬使，以奴李士貴為使宅十將兵馬使，劉守義、劉襯忠、董可武、崔玄度分將牙兵。

translations.literal: He then plotted with staff members Zhang Gu and Chen Yangting to follow the example of the Hebei circuits, appointing his younger brother's son Zhen—son of Right Brave Guard General Congsu—as Inner Gate Military Commissioner, his nephew Kuangzhou as Central Army Military Commissioner, clerk Wang Xie as Personal Military Commissioner of the Escort Guard, his slave Li Shigui as Military Commissioner of the Ten Household Guards of the Commissioner's Residence, and Liu Shouyi, Liu Chenzhong, Dong Kewu, and Cui Xuandu to command the guard troops in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted with staff members Zhang Gu and Chen Yangting to follow the Hebei model: he made his nephew Zhen—son of his brother Right Brave Guard General Congsu—Inner Gate military commissioner; his nephew Kuangzhou central army commissioner; clerk Wang Xie personal military commissioner of the escort guard; his slave Li Shigui military commissioner of the commissioner's household guard; and Liu Shouyi, Liu Chenzhong, Dong Kewu, and Cui Xuandu each took command of part of the guard force.

sentences.zh: 谷，鄆州人，揚庭，洪州人也。

translations.literal: Gu was a man of Yanzhou; Yangting was a man of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was from Yanzhou; Yangting was from Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 從諫尋薨，稹秘不發喪。

translations.literal: Congjian soon died; Zhen kept the death secret and did not announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian soon died, and Zhen kept the death secret without announcing mourning.

sentences.zh: 王協為稹謀曰：「正當如寶歷年樣為之，不出百日，旌節自至。

translations.literal: Wang Xie plotted for Zhen, saying: "We should do exactly as in the Baoli era; within a hundred days the command baton and credentials will arrive of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xie advised Zhen, "We should handle this exactly as in the Baoli reign. Within a hundred days the imperial commission will arrive on its own.

sentences.zh: 但嚴奉監軍，厚遺敕使，四境勿出兵，城中暗為備而已。」

translations.literal: Only strictly honor the army supervisor, richly reward the imperial envoy, send no troops beyond the borders, and quietly prepare defenses within the city."
translations.idiomatic: All we need do is treat the army supervisor with strict respect, richly reward the imperial envoy, keep our troops inside the borders, and quietly prepare the city defenses."

sentences.zh: 使押牙姜崟奏求國醫，上遣中使解朝政以醫往問疾。

translations.literal: He had the escort guard officer Jiang Yin memorialize requesting an imperial physician; the emperor sent the palace envoy Xie Chaozheng with a doctor to inquire after the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had escort officer Jiang Yin memorialize for an imperial physician. The emperor sent palace envoy Xie Chaozheng with a doctor to inquire after Congjian's condition.

sentences.zh: 稹又逼監軍崔士康奏稱從諫疾病，請命其子稹為留後。

translations.literal: Zhen also forced army supervisor Cui Shikang to memorialize that Congjian was ill and to request that his son Zhen be appointed acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen also forced army supervisor Cui Shikang to report that Congjian was ill and to ask that his son Zhen be made acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上遣供奉官薛士幹往諭指云：「恐從諫疾未平，宜且就東部療之；

translations.literal: The emperor sent the palace attendant Xue Shigan to convey the imperial intent, saying: "I fear Congjian's illness is not yet settled; he should go to the eastern capital for treatment for the time being;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent palace attendant Xue Shigan with instructions: "I fear Congjian's illness is not yet over. He should go to the eastern capital for treatment for now;

sentences.zh: 俟稍瘳，別有任使。

translations.literal: when he has recovered somewhat, another appointment will be made.
translations.idiomatic: when he has recovered somewhat, another appointment will be made for him.

sentences.zh: 仍遣稹入朝，必厚加官爵。」

translations.literal: Zhen should also be sent to court and will surely receive generous rank and titles."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen should also come to court, and he will surely receive generous honors."

sentences.zh: 上以澤潞事謀於宰相，宰相多以為：「回鶻餘燼未滅，邊鄙猶須警備，復討澤潞，國力不支，請以劉稹權知軍事。」

translations.literal: The emperor consulted the chief ministers about the Zelu affair; most ministers held: "The Uyghur embers are not yet extinguished and the frontier still needs vigilance; to campaign again against Zelu would overstrain the state's strength. We ask that Liu Zhen be temporarily put in charge of military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his chief ministers about Zelu. Most argued, "The Uyghur remnants are not yet destroyed and the frontier still needs guarding. Another campaign against Zelu would overstrain the empire. Liu Zhen should be allowed to act as military commissioner for the time being."

sentences.zh: 諫官及群臣上言者亦然。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials and other courtiers who submitted opinions said the same.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials and other courtiers who spoke up agreed.

sentences.zh: 李德裕獨曰：「澤潞事體與河朔三鎮不同。

translations.literal: Li Deyu alone said: "The Zelu situation is not the same as that of the three Hebei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu alone argued, "The Zelu situation is not the same as that of the three Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 河朔習亂已久，人心難化。

translations.literal: Hebei has long been accustomed to rebellion, and its people's hearts are hard to transform.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei has long been accustomed to rebellion, and its people are hard to change.

sentences.zh: 是故累朝以來，置之度外。

translations.literal: Therefore for successive reigns it has been placed beyond regular control.
translations.idiomatic: That is why successive reigns have treated it as beyond ordinary control.

sentences.zh: 澤潞近處心腹，一軍素稱忠義，嘗破走朱滔，擒盧從史。

translations.literal: Zelu lies close to the heartland; its army has always been called loyal and righteous, having once routed Zhu Tao and captured Lu Congshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zelu lies close to the heartland. Its army has always been counted loyal and righteous—it once routed Zhu Tao and captured Lu Congshi.

sentences.zh: 頃時多用儒臣為帥，如李抱真成立此軍，德宗猶不許承襲，使李緘護喪歸東都。

translations.literal: In those days civil officials were often made commanders; when Li Baozhen founded this army, Emperor Dezong still would not allow succession and had Li Qian escort the coffin back to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In those days civil officials often commanded it. When Li Baozhen founded this army, even Emperor Dezong refused hereditary succession and had Li Qian escort the coffin back to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 敬宗不恤國務，宰相又無遠略，劉悟之死，因循以授從諫。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong neglected state affairs, and the chief ministers lacked long-range vision; when Liu Wu died, they drifted along and granted command to Congjian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong neglected state affairs, and the chief ministers lacked foresight. When Liu Wu died, they simply drifted along and gave the command to Congjian.

sentences.zh: 從諫跋扈難制，累上表迫脅朝廷，今垂死之際，復以兵權擅付豎子。

translations.literal: Congjian was overbearing and hard to control, repeatedly submitting memorials to coerce the court; now on his deathbed he again arrogantly hands military power to a stripling.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was overbearing and hard to control and repeatedly coerced the court with memorials. Now, on his deathbed, he arrogantly hands military power to a stripling.

sentences.zh: 朝廷若又因而授之，則四方諸鎮誰不思效其所為，天子威令不復行矣！」

translations.literal: If the court again grants it on that basis, which of the four quarters' circuits would not think to imitate his conduct—the Son of Heaven's authority would no longer be enforced!"
translations.idiomatic: If the court grants this too, every circuit in the empire will think to do the same—and the emperor's authority will never be enforced again!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿以何術制之，果可克否？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "By what method would you control this—can it truly be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What method would you use to control this—and can it really be taken?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「稹所恃者河朔三鎮。

translations.literal: He replied: "What Zhen relies on are the three Hebei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Zhen relies on the three Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 但得鎮、魏不與之同。

translations.literal: If only Zhen and Wei do not join with him—
translations.idiomatic: If only Zhenzhou and Weibo do not join him—

sentences.zh: 則稹無能為也。

translations.literal: then Zhen can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: then Zhen can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 若遣重臣往諭王元逵、何弘敬，以河朔自艱難以來，列聖許其傳襲，已成故事，與澤潞不同。

translations.literal: If we send a senior minister to instruct Wang Yuankui and He Hongjing that since the time of hardship Hebei has been allowed hereditary succession by successive emperors and this has become established precedent, unlike Zelu—
translations.idiomatic: Send a senior minister to tell Wang Yuankui and He Hongjing that since the rebellions, successive emperors have allowed Hebei hereditary succession as established precedent—something Zelu is not.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷將加兵澤潞，不欲更出禁軍至山東。

translations.literal: now the court intends to send troops against Zelu and does not wish to dispatch imperial guards again to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: The court now means to send troops against Zelu and does not wish to dispatch imperial guards to Shandong again.

sentences.zh: 其山東三州隸昭義者，委兩鎮攻之。

translations.literal: The three Shandong prefectures under Zhaoyi should be entrusted to the two circuits to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The three Shandong prefectures under Zhaoyi should be left to the two circuits to attack.

sentences.zh: 兼令遍諭將士，以賊平之日厚加官賞。

translations.literal: At the same time, let it be proclaimed throughout to officers and soldiers that when the rebels are pacified generous ranks and rewards will be granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, tell all officers and soldiers that when the rebels are crushed they will receive generous honors and rewards.

sentences.zh: 苟兩鎮聽命，不從旁沮橈官軍，則稹必成擒矣！」

translations.literal: If the two circuits obey and do not obstruct the imperial army from the side, then Zhen will surely be captured!"
translations.idiomatic: If the two circuits obey and do not obstruct the imperial army, Zhen will surely be captured!"

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「吾與德裕同之，保無後悔。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "I agree with Deyu; I guarantee there will be no regret."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "I agree with Deyu. I guarantee we will not regret this."

sentences.zh: 遂決意討稹，群臣言者不復入矣。

translations.literal: He thereupon resolved to campaign against Zhen, and those among the ministers who had spoken were heard no more.
translations.idiomatic: He resolved to campaign against Zhen, and the ministers who had opposed the idea were heard no more.

sentences.zh: 上命德裕草詔賜成德節度使王元逵、魏博節度使何弘敬，其略曰：「澤潞一鎮，與卿事體不同，勿為子孫之謀，欲存輔車之勢。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Deyu to draft edicts bestowed upon Wang Yuankui, military commissioner of Chengde, and He Hongjing, military commissioner of Weibo. The gist read: "The Zelu circuit differs in nature from your affairs; do not plot for your descendants or seek to preserve a cart-and-wheel alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Deyu to draft edicts for Wang Yuankui of Chengde and He Hongjing of Weibo. The gist was: "The Zelu circuit is not the same as yours. Do not plot for your descendants or try to preserve a mutual-support alliance.

sentences.zh: 但能顯立功效，自然福及後昆。」

translations.literal: If you only achieve clear merit, blessings will naturally reach your descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Achieve clear merit, and blessings will naturally reach your descendants."

sentences.zh: 丁丑，上臨朝，稱其語要切，曰：「當如此直告之是也！」

translations.literal: On dingchou, the emperor held court and praised the language as essential and direct, saying: "This is how one should speak plainly to them!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou the emperor held court and praised the wording as sharp and direct. "That is how they should be told plainly!"

sentences.zh: 又賜張仲武詔，以「回鶻餘燼未滅，塞上多虞，專委卿禦侮。」

translations.literal: An edict was also bestowed upon Zhang Zhongwu, stating: "The Uyghur embers are not yet extinguished and the frontier has many alarms; you alone are entrusted with repelling insult."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Zhang Zhongwu an edict saying, "The Uyghur remnants are not yet destroyed and the frontier remains unsettled. You alone are entrusted with its defense."

sentences.zh: 元逵、弘敬得詔，悚息聽命。

translations.literal: Yuankui and Hongjing received the edicts and, trembling, obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankui and Hongjing received the edicts and obeyed in fear.

sentences.zh: 解朝政至上黨，劉稹見朝政曰：「相公危困，不任拜詔。」

translations.literal: Xie Chaozheng reached Shangdang; Liu Zhen, seeing Chaozheng, said: "The commissioner is gravely ill and cannot receive the edict."
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Chaozheng reached Shangdang, Liu Zhen told him, "The commissioner is gravely ill and cannot receive the edict."

sentences.zh: 朝政欲突入，兵馬使劉武德、董可武躡簾而立，朝政恐有他變。

translations.literal: Chaozheng tried to push his way in; military commissioners Liu Wude and Dong Kewu stepped behind the curtain and stood there. Chaozheng feared some other turn of events.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozheng tried to enter anyway. Military commissioners Liu Wude and Dong Kewu stepped behind the curtain to block him. Chaozheng feared trouble.

sentences.zh: 遽走出。

translations.literal: He hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: He fled at once.

sentences.zh: 稹贈贐直數千緡，復遣牙將梁叔文入謝。

translations.literal: Zhen gave several thousand strings of cash as funeral gifts and again sent guard officer Liang Shuwen in to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen sent several thousand strings of cash as gifts and dispatched guard officer Liang Shuwen to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 薛士幹入境，俱不問從諫之疾，直為已知其死之意。

translations.literal: When Xue Shigan entered the territory, none inquired about Congjian's illness—it was directly taken that they already knew he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Shigan entered the territory, no one even asked about Congjian's illness—it was plain they already knew he was dead.

sentences.zh: 都押牙郭誼等乃大出軍，至龍泉驛迎候敕使，請用河朔事體。

translations.literal: Chief escort guard Guo Yi and others then brought out the army in force to Longquan Post to welcome the imperial envoy and requested the Hebei protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Chief escort officer Guo Yi and others then marched out in force to Longquan Post to meet the imperial envoy and demanded Hebei-style protocol.

sentences.zh: 又見監軍言之，崔士康懦怯，不敢違。

translations.literal: They also spoke to the army supervisor about it; Cui Shikang was timid and did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: They said the same to army supervisor Cui Shikang, who was too timid to refuse.

sentences.zh: 於是將吏扶稹出見士眾，發喪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officers supported Zhen out to appear before the troops and announced mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The officers then brought Zhen out before the troops and announced mourning.

sentences.zh: 士幹竟不得入牙門，稹亦不受敕命。

translations.literal: Shigan in the end could not enter the headquarters gate, and Zhen also did not accept the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Shigan never entered the headquarters gate, and Zhen refused the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 誼，兗州人也。

translations.literal: Yi was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 解朝政覆命，上怒，杖之，配恭陵。

translations.literal: Xie Chaozheng reported back; the emperor was angry, had him beaten with the staff, and sent him to serve at Gongling.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Chaozheng reported back, the emperor was furious, had him beaten, and sent him to serve at Gongling.

sentences.zh: 囚姜崟、梁叔文。

translations.literal: Jiang Yin and Liang Shuwen were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yin and Liang Shuwen were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，始為從諫輟朝，贈太傅，詔劉稹護喪歸東都。

translations.literal: On xinsi, mourning for Congjian was first announced at court; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and Liu Zhen was ordered to escort the coffin back to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi the court finally suspended audience for Congjian's mourning, posthumously made him Grand Tutor, and ordered Liu Zhen to escort the coffin to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 又召見劉從素，令以書諭稹，稹不從。

translations.literal: Liu Congsu was again summoned and ordered to write instructing Zhen; Zhen would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congsu was summoned and told to write instructing Zhen, but Zhen refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以忠武節度使王茂元為河陽節度使，邠寧節度使王宰為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Wang Maoyuan, military commissioner of Zhongwu, was made military commissioner of Heyang, and Wang Zai, military commissioner of Binning, was made military commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai, Wang Maoyuan of Zhongwu was made military commissioner of Heyang, and Wang Zai of Binning was made military commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 茂元，棲曜之子；

translations.literal: Maoyuan was the son of Qi Yao;
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan was the son of Qi Yao;

sentences.zh: 宰，智興之子也。

translations.literal: Zai was the son of Zhi Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was the son of Zhi Xing.

sentences.zh: 黃州刺史杜牧上李德裕書，自言：「嘗問淮西將董重制以三州之眾四歲不破之由，重質以為由朝廷徵兵太雜，客軍數少，既不能自成一軍，事須貼付地主。

translations.literal: Du Mu, prefect of Huangzhou, sent Li Deyu a letter saying of himself: "I once asked the Huaixi general Dong Chongzhi why three circuits' forces could not break them in four years. Chongzhi held that because the court's mobilization was too mixed and the guest armies too few to form independent forces, they had to be attached to local commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Du Mu, prefect of Huangzhou, wrote Li Deyu a letter saying, "I once asked the Huaixi general Dong Chongzhi why three circuits' armies could not break the rebels in four years. Chongzhi said the court's mobilization was too mixed: the guest armies were too few to fight as independent forces and had to be attached to local commanders.

sentences.zh: 勢贏力弱，心志不一，多致敗亡。

translations.literal: Their position was strong but their strength weak, their wills not united—this often led to defeat and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers looked strong but force was weak and minds were divided—so defeat followed.

sentences.zh: 故初戰二年以來，戰則必勝，是多殺客軍。

translations.literal: Therefore in the first two years of fighting, whenever they fought they were sure to win—this was because they killed many guest troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first two years of fighting they won every battle—because they were killing guest troops in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 及二年已後，客軍殫少，止與陳許、河陽全軍相搏，縱使唐州兵不能因虛取城，蔡州事力亦不支矣。

translations.literal: After the second year the guest armies were nearly exhausted; they fought only the full armies of Chenxu and Heyang. Even if Tangzhou troops could not seize cities by exploiting gaps, Caizhou's strength could no longer hold out.
translations.idiomatic: After the second year the guest armies were nearly gone, and the rebels fought only the full Chenxu and Heyang armies. Even if Tangzhou troops could not exploit openings to take cities, Caizhou's strength could no longer hold.

sentences.zh: 其時朝廷若使鄂州、壽州、唐州只保境，不用進戰，但用陳許、鄭滑兩道全軍，貼以宣、潤弩手，令其守隘，即不出一歲，無蔡州矣。

translations.literal: If at that time the court had had Ezhou, Shouzhou, and Tangzhou hold their borders without advancing, and used only the full armies of the Chenxu and Zheng-Hua circuits supplemented with crossbowmen from Xuan and Run, ordering them to guard the passes, Caizhou would have fallen within a year.
translations.idiomatic: If the court had then kept Ezhou, Shouzhou, and Tangzhou on the defensive and used only the full Chenxu and Zheng-Hua armies, supplemented with crossbowmen from Xuan and Run, to hold the passes, Caizhou would have fallen within a year.

sentences.zh: 今者上黨之叛，復與淮西不同。

translations.literal: The present rebellion at Shangdang is again different from Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: The present rebellion at Shangdang is different again from Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 淮西為寇僅五十歲，其人味為寇之腴，見為寇之利，風俗益固，氣焰已成，自以為天下之兵莫與我敵，根深源闊，取之固難。

translations.literal: Huaixi had been bandits for only fifty years; its people had tasted the fat of banditry and seen the profit of rebellion. Custom grew firmer, arrogance took shape, and they believed no army under Heaven could match them. Roots were deep and sources broad—taking them was inherently hard.
translations.idiomatic: Huaixi had been in rebellion for only fifty years, yet its people had tasted the profits of banditry, custom had hardened, and arrogance had set in. They believed no army under Heaven could match them. With deep roots and broad support, they were inherently hard to take.

sentences.zh: 夫上黨則不然。

translations.literal: Shangdang is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdang is not like that.

sentences.zh: 自安、史南下，不甚附柰；

translations.literal: Since An and Shi marched south, it did not much attach to them;
translations.idiomatic: Since An and Shi marched south, it did not readily join the rebellion;

sentences.zh: 建中之後，每奮忠義。

translations.literal: after the Jianzhong era it repeatedly exerted loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: and after the Jianzhong era it repeatedly showed loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 是以郳公抱真能窘田悅，走朱滔，常以孤窮寒苦之軍，橫折河朔強梁之眾。

translations.literal: Therefore Duke of Xing, Baozhen, could distress Tian Yue and rout Zhu Tao, often using a lonely, poor, and hard-pressed army to break across the strong hosts of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: That is how Duke of Xing Li Baozhen could corner Tian Yue and rout Zhu Tao—often using a poor, isolated army to break the strongest forces of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 以此證驗，人心忠赤，習尚專一，可以盡見。

translations.literal: By this proof, the people's hearts are loyal and red, their customs single-minded—this can fully be seen.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the people's hearts remain loyal and their customs upright.

sentences.zh: 劉悟卒，從諫求繼，與扶同者，只鄆州隨來中軍二千耳。

translations.literal: When Liu Wu died, Congjian sought succession; those who supported him were only two thousand central-army men who had come from Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wu died, Congjian sought succession—and only two thousand central-army men who had come from Yanzhou supported him.

sentences.zh: 值寶歷多故，因以授之。

translations.literal: It happened amid the many troubles of the Baoli reign, and so command was granted him.
translations.idiomatic: The Baoli reign was troubled, and so command was granted him.

sentences.zh: 今才二十餘歲，風俗未改，故老尚存，雖欲劫之，必不用命。

translations.literal: Now barely twenty years have passed; custom is unchanged and old veterans still live. Even if one wished to coerce them, they would surely not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Barely twenty years have passed. Custom is unchanged and old veterans still live. Even if Zhen tries to coerce them, they will not obey.

sentences.zh: 今成德、魏博雖盡節效順，亦不過圍一城，攻一堡，係累稚老而已。

translations.literal: Now even if Chengde and Weibo exert full loyalty and obedience, they will do no more than besiege one city and assault one fort, capturing women, children, and the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Chengde and Weibo give full loyalty, they will do no more than besiege a city or assault a fort and capture women, children, and the aged.

sentences.zh: 若使河陽萬人為壘，窒天井之口，高壁深塹，勿與之戰。

translations.literal: If ten thousand Heyang troops built fortifications, blocked the mouth of Tianjing Pass, raised high walls and deep ditches, and did not give battle—
translations.idiomatic: If ten thousand Heyang troops fortify the mouth of Tianjing Pass with high walls and deep ditches and refuse battle—

sentences.zh: 只以忠武、武寧兩軍，貼以青州五千精甲，宣、潤二千弩手，逕搗上黨，不過數月，必覆其巢穴矣！」

translations.literal: and only the Zhongwu and Wuning armies, supplemented with five thousand elite armored troops from Qingzhou and two thousand crossbowmen from Xuan and Run, struck straight at Shangdang—in no more than a few months their nest would surely be overturned!"
translations.idiomatic: and the Zhongwu and Wuning armies, supplemented with five thousand elite armored troops from Qingzhou and two thousand crossbowmen from Xuan and Run, strike straight at Shangdang—in a few months their stronghold will surely fall!"

sentences.zh: 時德裕制置澤潞，亦頗采牧言。

translations.literal: At that time, as Deyu arranged matters in Zelu, he also largely adopted Mu's words.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Deyu arranged the Zelu campaign, he largely adopted Du Mu's advice.

sentences.zh: 上雖外尊寵仇士良，內實忌惡之。

translations.literal: Although outwardly the emperor honored and favored Qiu Shiliang, inwardly he truly resented and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly the emperor honored Qiu Shiliang, but inwardly he resented him.

sentences.zh: 士良頗覺之，遂以老病求散秩，詔以左衛上將軍兼內侍監、知省事。

translations.literal: Shiliang somewhat perceived this and thereupon, citing old age and illness, requested a nominal post; an edict made him General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, concurrently Palace Domestic Supervisor, with charge of palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang sensed this and, citing old age and illness, asked for a nominal post. An edict made him General-in-Chief of the Left Guard while retaining him as Palace Domestic Supervisor in charge of palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 李德裕言於上曰：「議者皆雲劉悟有功，稹未可亟誅，宜全恩禮。

translations.literal: Li Deyu said to the emperor: "Those who discuss the matter all say Liu Wu had merit and Zhen should not be quickly punished; full favor and courtesy should be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu told the emperor, "Those who discuss this say Liu Wu had merit and Zhen should not be punished hastily—they urge full courtesy instead.

sentences.zh: 請下百官議，以盡人情。」

translations.literal: I ask that the matter be sent down for discussion among the officials to exhaust all human sentiment."
translations.idiomatic: Send the matter down for discussion among the officials so that public sentiment is fully heard."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「悟亦何功，當時迫於救死耳，非素心徇國也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What merit did Wu have? At the time he was forced to save his life—that was not a lifelong heart devoted to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "What merit did Wu have? At the time he was saving his own life—that was not lifelong devotion to the state.

sentences.zh: 籍使有功，父子為將相二十餘年，國家報之足矣，稹何得復自言！

translations.literal: Even if he had merit, father and son served as generals and ministers for more than twenty years—the state has repaid them enough. How can Zhen speak for himself again!
translations.idiomatic: Even if he had merit, father and son served as generals and ministers for more than twenty years—the state has repaid them enough. How can Zhen claim the command for himself!

sentences.zh: 朕以為凡有功當顯賞，有罪亦不可苟免也。」

translations.literal: I hold that wherever there is merit there should be clear reward, and wherever there is guilt it cannot be casually exempted."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that merit deserves clear reward, and guilt cannot be casually forgiven."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「陛下之言，誠得理國之要。」

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Your Majesty's words truly grasp the essentials of governing the state."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "Your Majesty's words truly grasp the essentials of governing the state."

sentences.zh: 五月，李德裕言太子賓客、分司李宗閔與劉從諫交通，不宜置之東都。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Li Deyu said that Li Zongmin, Crown Prince's Guest serving at the secondary capital, had dealings with Liu Congjian and should not be kept in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Li Deyu said that Li Zongmin, Crown Prince's Guest at the secondary capital, had dealings with Liu Congjian and should not remain in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以宗閔為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Zongmin was made prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, Li Zongmin was made prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使王茂元以步騎三千守萬善；

translations.literal: Wang Maoyuan, military commissioner of Heyang, garrisoned Wanshan with three thousand infantry and cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyuan of Heyang garrisoned Wanshan with three thousand infantry and cavalry;

sentences.zh: 河東節度使劉沔步騎二千守芒車關，步兵一千五百軍榆社；

translations.literal: Liu Mian, military commissioner of Hedong, garrisoned Mangche Pass with two thousand infantry and cavalry and stationed fifteen hundred foot soldiers at Yushe;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian of Hedong garrisoned Mangche Pass with two thousand infantry and cavalry and stationed fifteen hundred foot soldiers at Yushe;

sentences.zh: 成德節度使王元逵以步騎三千守臨洺，掠堯山；

translations.literal: Wang Yuankui, military commissioner of Chengde, garrisoned Linming with three thousand infantry and cavalry and raided Yaoshan;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui of Chengde garrisoned Linming with three thousand infantry and cavalry and raided Yaoshan;

sentences.zh: 河中節度使陳夷行以步騎一千守翼城，步兵五百益冀氏。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing, military commissioner of Hezhong, garrisoned Yicheng with one thousand infantry and cavalry and added five hundred foot soldiers at Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing of Hezhong garrisoned Yicheng with one thousand infantry and cavalry and added five hundred foot soldiers at Jishi.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，制削奪劉從諫及子稹官爵，以元逵為澤潞北面招討使，何弘敬為南面招討使，與夷行、劉沔、茂元合力攻討。

translations.literal: On xinchou, by decree the ranks and titles of Liu Congjian and his son Zhen were stripped; Yuankui was made northern campaign commissioner against Zelu, Hongjing southern campaign commissioner, and together with Yixing, Liu Mian, and Maoyuan they were to attack jointly.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou an edict stripped Liu Congjian and his son Zhen of rank and titles. Yuankui was made northern campaign commissioner against Zelu, Hongjing southern campaign commissioner, and together with Yixing, Liu Mian, and Maoyuan they were to attack jointly.

sentences.zh: 先是河北諸鎮有自立者，朝廷必先有弔祭使，次冊贈使、宣慰使繼往商度軍情。

translations.literal: Previously, when a Hebei circuit installed its own commander, the court would first send a mourning envoy, then investiture and condolence envoys and pacification envoys in succession to assess army sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when a Hebei circuit installed its own commander, the court would first send a mourning envoy, then investiture, condolence, and pacification envoys in succession to gauge army sentiment.

sentences.zh: 必不可與節，則別除一官；

translations.literal: If the command baton absolutely could not be granted, another office would be separately appointed;
translations.idiomatic: If the commission absolutely could not be granted, another office would be appointed instead;

sentences.zh: 俟軍中不聽出，然後始用兵。

translations.literal: only when the army would not obey would troops finally be deployed.
translations.idiomatic: and only when the army refused to obey would troops finally be deployed.

sentences.zh: 故常及半歲，軍中得繕完為備。

translations.literal: Therefore it often took half a year, giving the army time to repair and prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: This often took half a year, giving the army time to repair defenses and prepare.

sentences.zh: 至是，宰相亦欲且遣使開諭，上即命下詔討之。

translations.literal: On this occasion the chief ministers also wished first to send envoys to open negotiations, but the emperor immediately ordered an edict of campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: This time the chief ministers also wanted to send envoys first, but the emperor immediately ordered an edict of campaign.

sentences.zh: 王元逵受詔之日，出師屯趙州。

translations.literal: On the day Wang Yuankui received the edict, he marched out and encamped at Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The day Wang Yuankui received the edict, he marched out and encamped at Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以翰林學士承旨崔鉉為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On renyin, Cui Xuan, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal to the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Cui Xuan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 鉉，元略之子也。

translations.literal: Xuan was the son of Yuanlue.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan was the son of Yuanlue.

sentences.zh: 上夜召學士韋琮，以鉉名授之，令草制，宰相、樞密皆不之知。

translations.literal: At night the emperor summoned Academician Wei Cong, gave him Xuan's name, and ordered him to draft the appointment edict; neither the chief ministers nor the privy council knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor summoned Academician Wei Cong, gave him Cui Xuan's name, and ordered him to draft the appointment edict—neither the chief ministers nor the privy council knew of it.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使劉行深、楊欽義皆願愨，不敢預事，老宦者尤之曰：「此由劉、楊懦怯，墮敗舊風故也。」

translations.literal: At the time the privy councilors Liu Xingshen and Yang Qinyi both wished to be prudent and did not dare to take part in affairs; old eunuchs blamed them, saying: "This is because Liu and Yang are cowardly and weak and have ruined the old ways."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Privy Councilors Liu Xingshen and Yang Qinyi both preferred to keep their heads down and would not intervene in affairs. Older eunuchs blamed them, saying, "This is because Liu and Yang are cowardly and have ruined the old ways."

sentences.zh: 悰，乾度之子也。

translations.literal: Cong was the son of Qiandu.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was the son of Qiandu.

sentences.zh: 以武寧節度使李彥佐為晉絳行營諸軍節度招討使。

translations.literal: Li Yanzuo, military commissioner of Wuning, was made commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of the Jin- and Jiang-linked campaign headquarters of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzuo, military commissioner of Wuning, was appointed commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of the Jin-Jiang campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 劉沔自代州還太原。

translations.literal: Liu Mian returned from Dai Prefecture to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian returned from Dai Prefecture to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 築望仙台於禁中。

translations.literal: The Platform for Viewing Immortals was built within the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: The Platform for Viewing Immortals was built inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 六月，王茂元遣兵馬使馬繼等將步騎二千軍於天井關南科斗店，劉稹遣衙內十將薛茂卿將親軍二千拒之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wang Maoyuan sent Cavalry Commander Ma Ji and others to lead two thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison at Kedou Post south of Tianjing Pass; Liu Zhen sent Palace Inner Ten-General Xue Maoqing to lead two thousand personal troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Wang Maoyuan sent Cavalry Commander Ma Ji and others with two thousand infantry and cavalry to hold Kedou Post south of Tianjing Pass. Liu Zhen sent Palace Inner General Xue Maoqing with two thousand personal troops to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯可汗遣將軍溫仵合入貢。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz khan sent General Wenwuhe to enter court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Kirghiz khan sent General Wenwuhe to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 上賜之書，諭以速平回鶻、黑車子，乃遣使行冊命。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed a letter upon him, instructing him to speedily pacify the Uyghurs and the Heichezi, and then sent envoys to carry out the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him a letter instructing him to speedily pacify the Uyghurs and the Heichezi, then dispatched envoys to invest him formally.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，仇士良以左衛上將軍、內侍監致仕。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Qiu Shiliang retired with the posts of General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and Palace Domestic Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiyou, Qiu Shiliang retired as General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and Palace Domestic Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 其黨送歸私第，士良教以固權寵之術曰：「天子不可令閒，常宜以奢靡娛其耳目，使日新月盛，無暇更及它事，然後吾輩可以得志。

translations.literal: His faction escorted him back to his private residence. Shiliang taught them the art of securing power and favor, saying: "The Son of Heaven must not be allowed leisure. One should constantly entertain his eyes and ears with extravagance and dissipation, making them grow daily more abundant so that he has no time to turn to other matters; then our sort can have our way.
translations.idiomatic: His followers escorted him home. Shiliang taught them how to hold on to power: "Never let the emperor have idle time. Keep his eyes and ears filled with luxury and pleasure, day after day, until he has no room for anything else—then men like us can do as we please.

sentences.zh: 慎勿使之讀書，親近儒生，彼見前代興亡，心知憂懼，則吾蜚疏斥矣。」

translations.literal: Be careful never to let him read books or draw near Confucian scholars. If he sees the rise and fall of former ages and knows worry and fear in his heart, then we will be slandered, estranged, and cast out."
translations.idiomatic: Never let him read books or keep company with Confucian scholars. If he sees how dynasties rise and fall and learns to worry, we will be slandered and driven out."

sentences.zh: 其黨拜謝而去。

translations.literal: His faction bowed in thanks and departed.
translations.idiomatic: His followers bowed in thanks and left.

sentences.zh: 丙子，詔王元逵、李彥佐、劉沔、王茂元、何弘敬以七月中旬五道齊進，劉稹求降皆不得受。

translations.literal: On bingzi, an edict ordered Wang Yuankui, Li Yanzuo, Liu Mian, Wang Maoyuan, and He Hongjing to advance together along five routes in mid-seventh month; none of Liu Zhen's requests to surrender were to be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, an edict ordered Wang Yuankui, Li Yanzuo, Liu Mian, Wang Maoyuan, and He Hongjing to advance together along five routes in mid-seventh month. None of Liu Zhen's offers to surrender were to be accepted.

sentences.zh: 又詔劉沔自將兵取仰車關路以臨賊境。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Liu Mian personally to lead troops by the Yangche Pass route to press upon the rebel border.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered Liu Mian to lead troops personally along the Yangche Pass route to threaten the rebel border.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃鄯州節度使尚婢婢，世為吐蕃相，婢婢好讀書，不樂仕進，國人敬之。

translations.literal: Shang Bibi, military commissioner of Shan Prefecture in Tibet, came from a family that for generations had served as Tibetan chancellors. Bibi loved reading and did not delight in advancing in office; the people of the state respected her.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Bibi, Tibetan military commissioner of Shan Prefecture, came from a family that had produced chancellors for generations. She loved books and had no taste for office; her countrymen respected her.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，彝泰贊普強起之，使鎮鄯州。

translations.literal: When she was a little over forty, the zanpu Yitai forcibly raised her up and had her garrison Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When she was in her forties, Zanpu Yitai pressed her into service and posted her to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 婢婢寬厚沉勇，有謀略，訓練士卒多精勇。

translations.literal: Bibi was generous, steady, and brave, possessed of strategy, and in training soldiers produced many who were elite and valiant.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi was generous, resolute, and brave, skilled in strategy, and the troops she trained were many of them elite fighters.

sentences.zh: 論恐熱雖名義兵，實謀篡國，忌婢婢，恐襲其後，欲先滅之。

translations.literal: Although Lun Kongre styled his force a righteous army, in fact he plotted to usurp the state. He resented Bibi, feared she might strike from behind, and wished first to destroy her.
translations.idiomatic: Lun Kongre called his army a righteous force, but in truth he meant to seize power. He resented Bibi, feared an attack from the rear, and wanted to destroy her first.

sentences.zh: 是月，大舉兵擊婢婢，旌旗雜畜千里不絕。

translations.literal: That month he raised a great army to attack Bibi; banners, flags, and mixed livestock stretched unbroken for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: That month he marched in force against Bibi; banners, flags, and herds stretched unbroken for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 至鎮西，大風震電，天火燒殺裨將十餘人，雜畜以百數，恐熱惡之，盤桓不進。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhenxi, great wind, thunder, and heaven-sent fire burned and killed more than ten assistant generals and livestock by the hundreds. Kongre regarded this as ill-omened and lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenxi, violent wind and thunder brought fire from heaven that killed more than ten of his subordinate generals and hundreds of livestock. Kongre took this as a bad omen and halted without advancing.

sentences.zh: 婢婢謂其下曰：「恐熱之來，視我如螻蟻，以為不足屠也。

translations.literal: Bibi said to her subordinates: "Kongre's coming treats me like an ant and thinks me not worth the slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi told her officers, "Kongre comes treating me like an ant he need not bother to crush.

sentences.zh: 今遇天災，猶豫不進，吾不如迎伏以卻之，使其志益驕而不為備，然後可圖也。」

translations.literal: Now that he has met heaven's disaster and hesitates without advancing, I had better welcome him and submit to drive him back, making his ambition ever prouder so that he makes no preparations; then he can be taken in hand."
translations.idiomatic: Now heaven has struck him and he hangs back in doubt. Better to welcome him and feign submission, let his pride swell until he drops his guard—then we can strike."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使以金帛、牛酒犒師，且致書言：「相公舉義兵以匡國難，闔境之內，孰不向風！

translations.literal: Thereupon she sent envoys with gold, silks, cattle, and wine to reward the army, and also sent a letter saying: "The Lord Chancellor has raised a righteous army to set right the state's peril; within the whole circuit, who does not turn toward your wind!
translations.idiomatic: She sent envoys with gold, silks, cattle, and wine to reward his army, along with a letter: "You have raised a righteous army to save the realm—who in these lands would not rally to you?

sentences.zh: 苟遣一介，賜之折簡，敢不承命！

translations.literal: If you would send but one messenger and grant a brief letter, how would I dare not accept the command!
translations.idiomatic: Send but one messenger with a brief note, and I shall obey at once!

sentences.zh: 何必遠辱士眾，親臨下籓！

translations.literal: Why must you go so far as to humiliate your officers and soldiers by coming in person to this lower frontier!
translations.idiomatic: Why trouble your troops to march all this way to my humble border?

sentences.zh: 婢婢資性愚僻，惟嗜讀書，先贊普授以籓維，誠為非據，夙夜慚惕，惟求退居。

translations.literal: Bibi's nature is stupid and remote; she only loves reading. The former zanpu granted her frontier command, which truly was an unfitting post; day and night she feels shame and fear, and only seeks to withdraw and retire.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and unfit for command; I care only for books. The late zanpu gave me this frontier post undeservedly, and day and night I live in shame and fear, longing only to step aside.

sentences.zh: 相公若賜以骸骨，聽歸田骨，乃愜平生之素願也。」

translations.literal: If the Lord Chancellor would grant her old bones and permit her to return to her fields and homestead, that would satisfy her lifelong plain wish."
translations.idiomatic: If you would grant me retirement and let me return to my homestead, that would fulfill the wish I have held all my life.

sentences.zh: 恐熱得書喜，遍示諸將曰：「婢婢惟把書券，安知用兵！

translations.literal: Kongre received the letter with joy, showed it all around to his generals, and said: "Bibi only holds book scrolls—how would she know the use of arms!
translations.idiomatic: Kongre was delighted with the letter and showed it to all his generals. "Bibi knows only how to clutch book scrolls—what does she know of war!

sentences.zh: 待吾得國，當位以宰相，坐之於家，亦無所用也。」

translations.literal: When I obtain the state, I shall give her the rank of chancellor and seat her at home—she will be of no use even then."
translations.idiomatic: When I take the realm, I will make her chancellor and keep her at home—she will be good for nothing even then."

sentences.zh: 乃復為書，勤厚答之，引兵歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote again, answered her warmly and generously, and withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote back with warm courtesy and marched home.

sentences.zh: 婢婢聞之，撫髀笑曰：「我國無主，則歸大唐，豈能事此犬鼠乎！」

translations.literal: When Bibi heard of this, she slapped her thigh and laughed, saying: "If our state has no lord, then I shall return to Great Tang—how could I serve this dog or rat!"
translations.idiomatic: When Bibi heard this, she slapped her thigh and laughed. "If our country has no worthy ruler, I will go over to Great Tang. Why would I serve this cur?"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以山南東道節度使盧鈞為昭義節度招撫使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Lu Jun, military commissioner of the eastern circuit of Shannan, was made pacification commissioner of the Zhaoyi circuit.
