translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Lu Jun, military commissioner of eastern Shannan, was appointed pacification commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以鈞在襄陽寬厚有惠政，得眾心，故使領昭義以招懷之。

translations.literal: The court, because Jun in Xiangyang had been generous and had benevolent administration and had won the people's hearts, therefore had him take charge of Zhaoyi to win the people over.
translations.idiomatic: The court chose him because his generous rule in Xiangyang had won popular support, hoping he could win over Zhaoyi the same way.

sentences.zh: 上遣刑部侍郎兼御史中丞李回宣慰河北三鎮，令幽州乘秋早平回鶻，鎮、魏早平澤潞。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Li Hui, Vice Minister of Justice and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, to announce consolation to the three Hebei circuits, ordering Youzhou to take advantage of autumn to pacify the Uyghurs early and Zhen and Wei to pacify Zelu early.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Hui, Vice Minister of Justice and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, to reassure the three Hebei circuits, ordering Youzhou to crush the Uyghurs early that autumn and Zhen and Wei to finish off Zelu quickly.

sentences.zh: 回，太祖之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Hui was the eighth-generation descendant of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui was an eighth-generation descendant of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，李德裕言於上曰：「臣見向日河朔用兵，諸道利於出境仰給度支。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Li Deyu said to the emperor: "Your subject has seen that in past campaigns in Heshuo, the various circuits profited from crossing their borders and relying on the Department of Public Works for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen, Li Deyu told the emperor, "In past Heshuo campaigns, the various circuits profited from crossing their borders and living off central supply.

sentences.zh: 或陰與賊通，借一縣一柵據之，自以為功，坐食轉輸，延引歲時。

translations.literal: Some secretly communicated with the rebels, seized one county or one stockade and held it, took the credit for themselves, sat and ate from transport convoys, and dragged out the years.
translations.idiomatic: Some secretly colluded with the enemy, seized a county or stockade and called it a victory, then sat back eating convoy supplies and dragging the war out for years.

sentences.zh: 今請賜諸軍詔指，令王元逵取邢州，何弘敬取洺州，王茂元取澤州，李彥佐、劉沔取潞州，毋得取縣。」

translations.literal: Now I ask that edict instructions be bestowed upon the armies, ordering Wang Yuankui to take Xing Prefecture, He Hongjing to take Ming Prefecture, Wang Maoyuan to take Ze Prefecture, and Li Yanzuo and Liu Mian to take Lu Prefecture, and that they must not take counties."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that edicts go to every army: Wang Yuankui is to take Xing Prefecture, He Hongjing Ming Prefecture, Wang Maoyuan Ze Prefecture, and Li Yanzuo and Liu Mian Lu Prefecture—no seizing individual counties.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 晉絳行營節度使李彥佐自發徐州，行甚緩，又請休兵於絳州，兼請益兵。

translations.literal: Li Yanzuo, military commissioner of the Jin-Jiang campaign headquarters, after setting out from Xuzhou marched very slowly, and also requested to rest his troops at Jiang Prefecture while additionally asking for more soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzuo, commander of the Jin-Jiang campaign headquarters, left Xuzhou at a crawl, then asked to rest his troops at Jiang Prefecture and for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 李德裕言於上曰：「彥佐逗遛顧望，殊無討賊之意，所請皆不可許，宜賜詔切責，令進軍翼城。」

translations.literal: Li Deyu said to the emperor: "Yanzuo dawdles and looks about; he utterly lacks the will to attack the rebels. None of his requests should be granted. An edict should be bestowed sternly rebuking him and ordering him to advance his army to Yicheng."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu told the emperor, "Yanzuo is stalling and shows no real will to fight. Grant none of his requests. Send an edict rebuking him sharply and order him to advance on Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 德裕因請以天德防禦使石雄為彥佐之副，俟至軍中，令代之。

translations.literal: Deyu thereupon requested that Shi Xiong, defense commissioner of Tiande, be made Yanzuo's deputy, and that when he reached the army he be ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu also asked that Shi Xiong, defense commissioner of Tiande, be made Yanzuo's deputy with orders to replace him once he reached camp.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以雄為晉絳行營節度副使，仍詔彥佐進屯翼城。

translations.literal: On yisi, Xiong was made deputy military commissioner of the Jin-Jiang campaign headquarters, and Yanzuo was still ordered by edict to advance and encamp at Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, Shi Xiong was appointed deputy commander of the Jin-Jiang campaign headquarters, and Yanzuo was ordered to advance and encamp at Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 劉稹上表自陳：「亡父從諫為李訓雪冤，言仇士良罪惡，由此為權幸所疾，謂臣父潛懷異志，臣所以不敢舉族歸朝。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen submitted a memorial stating his case: "My deceased father Congjian cleared Li Xun's name and spoke of Qiu Shiliang's crimes; for this he was hated by the powerful and favored, who said my father secretly harbored rebellious intent. That is why I dare not bring my whole clan back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen memorialized in his own defense: "My late father Congjian vindicated Li Xun and denounced Qiu Shiliang's crimes. For that the powerful at court hated him and accused him of hidden disloyalty. That is why I dare not bring my whole clan back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下稍垂寬察，活臣一方！」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to extend a little lenient scrutiny and spare my one circuit!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to look on us with a little mercy and spare my circuit!

sentences.zh: 何弘敬亦為之奏雪，皆不報。

translations.literal: He Hongjing also memorialized to clear him; none received reply.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing also memorialized on his behalf. The court did not respond to either.

sentences.zh: 李回至河朔，何弘敬、王元逵、張仲武皆具橐鞬郊迎，立於道左，不敢令人控馬，讓制使先行，自兵興以來，未之有也。

translations.literal: When Li Hui reached Heshuo, He Hongjing, Wang Yuankui, and Zhang Zhongwu all went out to the suburbs with full military harness to welcome him, standing on the left of the road, not daring to have anyone hold their horses, yielding the road so the imperial commissioner went first—since the raising of armies, there had never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hui reached Heshuo, He Hongjing, Wang Yuankui, and Zhang Zhongwu all met him outside the city in full harness, standing to the side of the road without attendants to hold their horses, letting the imperial envoy pass first—nothing like it had been seen since the war began.

sentences.zh: 回明辯有膽氣，三鎮無不奉詔。

translations.literal: Hui was clear in argument and possessed of courage; none of the three circuits failed to obey the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui was sharp and bold, and all three circuits obeyed the edicts.

sentences.zh: 王元逵奏拔宣務柵，擊堯山。

translations.literal: Wang Yuankui memorialized that he had captured Xuannu Stockade and attacked Yaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui reported capturing Xuannu Stockade and attacking Yaoshan.

sentences.zh: 劉稹遣兵救堯山，元逵擊敗之，詔切責李彥佐、劉沔、王茂元，使速進兵逼賊境，且稱元逵之功以激厲之，加元逵同平章事。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen sent troops to rescue Yaoshan; Yuankui defeated them. An edict sternly rebuked Li Yanzuo, Liu Mian, and Wang Maoyuan, ordering them to advance their armies quickly to press the rebel border, and also praised Yuankui's merit to spur them on, adding Yuankui as Co-Equal to the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen sent troops to relieve Yaoshan; Yuankui routed them. An edict sharply rebuked Li Yanzuo, Liu Mian, and Wang Maoyuan and ordered them to press the rebel border at once. It also praised Yuankui's achievement to spur the others on and made him Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙丑，昭義大將李丕來降。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yichou, Li Pi, a great general of Zhaoyi, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day yichou, Li Pi, a senior Zhaoyi general, defected.

sentences.zh: 議者或謂賊故遣丕降，欲以疑誤官軍。

translations.literal: Some who discussed the matter said the rebels had deliberately sent Pi to surrender in order to sow doubt and mislead the government armies.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued the rebels had sent Pi deliberately to sow doubt and mislead the government armies.

sentences.zh: 李德裕言於上曰：「自用兵半年，未有降者，今安問誠之與詐？

translations.literal: Li Deyu said to the emperor: "Since arms were taken up half a year ago, there has been no defector; now why ask whether it is sincerity or deception?
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu told the emperor, "We have had no defectors in six months of fighting—why now ask whether this is sincere or a trick?

sentences.zh: 且須厚賞以勸將來，但不可置之要地耳。」

translations.literal: For the time being we must reward him generously to encourage those who will come later, but he must not be placed in a key post."
translations.idiomatic: Reward him generously to encourage others—but do not give him a critical post."

sentences.zh: 上從容言：「文宗好聽外議，諫官言事多不著名，有如匿名書。」

translations.literal: The emperor said at leisure: "Emperor Wenzong liked to listen to outside opinion; remonstrating officials often spoke on affairs without signing their names, as though it were an anonymous letter."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked casually, "Emperor Wenzong liked to heed outside opinion. Remonstrating officials often spoke without signing their names, as if writing anonymous letters.

sentences.zh: 李德裕曰：「臣頃在中書，文宗猶不爾。

translations.literal: Li Deyu said: "When your subject was recently in the Secretariat, Wenzong was still not like this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "When I was in the Secretariat, Wenzong had not yet been like that.

sentences.zh: 此乃李訓、鄭注教文宗以術御下，遂成此風。

translations.literal: This is Li Xun and Zheng Zhu teaching Wenzong the art of controlling subordinates by technique, and so this custom was formed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu taught Wenzong tricks for controlling his ministers—that is how this habit took hold.

sentences.zh: 人主但當推誠任人，有欺罔者，威以明刑，孰敢哉！」

translations.literal: A ruler need only extend sincerity and employ men; where there is deception, let clear punishments awe them—who would dare!"
translations.idiomatic: A ruler should simply trust his men openly. Let clear punishment fall on anyone who deceives him—who would dare?

sentences.zh: 上善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 王元逵前鋒入邢州境已逾月，何弘敬猶未出師，元逵屢有密表，稱弘敬懷兩端。

translations.literal: Wang Yuankui's vanguard had entered Xing Prefecture territory for more than a month, yet He Hongjing still had not marched out. Yuankui repeatedly sent secret memorials saying Hongjing harbored two minds.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui's vanguard had been inside Xing Prefecture for more than a month, but He Hongjing still had not marched. Yuankui sent repeated secret memorials accusing Hongjing of wavering.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，李德裕上言：「忠武累戰有功，軍聲頗振。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Li Deyu submitted: "Zhongwu has repeatedly fought with merit and its military reputation is quite vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao, Li Deyu submitted, "Zhongwu has fought well again and again, and its military reputation is strong.

sentences.zh: 王宰年力方壯，謀略可稱。

translations.literal: Wang Zai's years and strength are just in their prime, and his strategy can be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai is young and vigorous, and his strategy is sound.

sentences.zh: 請賜弘敬詔，以『河陽、河東皆閡山險，未能進軍，賊屢出兵焚掠晉、絳。

translations.literal: I ask that an edict be bestowed upon Hongjing, reading: "Heyang and Hedong are both blocked by mountain peril and have been unable to advance their armies; the rebels have repeatedly sent troops out to burn and plunder Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Send Hongjing an edict saying, "Heyang and Hedong are blocked by mountains and cannot advance. The rebels keep raiding Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 今遣王宰將忠武全軍徑魏博，直抵磁州，以分賊勢。』

translations.literal: Now Wang Zai is being sent to lead the full army of Zhongwu straight through Weibo and directly to Ci Prefecture, in order to divide the rebels' strength."
translations.idiomatic: We are sending Wang Zai with the full Zhongwu army through Weibo straight to Ci Prefecture to split the rebel force."

sentences.zh: 弘敬必懼，此攻心伐謀之術也。」

translations.literal: Hongjing will certainly be afraid—this is the art of attacking the heart and cutting down plans."
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing will be terrified. That is the art of attacking the mind rather than the field."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔宰悉選步騎精兵自相、魏趣磁州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zai to select all elite infantry and cavalry from Xiang and Wei and hurry to Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Zai to take the best infantry and cavalry from Xiang and Wei and march on Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，薛茂卿破科斗寨，擒河陽大將馬繼等，焚掠小寨一十七，距懷州才十餘里。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Xue Maoqing broke Kedou Stockade, captured Heyang great general Ma Ji and others, burned and plundered seventeen small stockades, and was only a little more than ten li from Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Xue Maoqing stormed Kedou Stockade, captured Heyang general Ma Ji and others, burned seventeen outposts, and came within little more than ten li of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 茂卿以無劉稹之命，故不敢入。

translations.literal: Maoqing, because he had no order from Liu Zhen, therefore did not dare to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqing lacked orders from Liu Zhen and did not dare advance farther.

sentences.zh: 時議者鼎沸，以為劉悟有功，不可絕其嗣。

translations.literal: At the time discussants boiled over, holding that Liu Wu had merit and his line must not be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: At court opinion boiled over: Liu Wu had done the empire a service, and his line must not be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 又，從諫養精兵十萬，糧支十年，如何可取！

translations.literal: Moreover, Congjian maintained a hundred thousand elite troops and provisions enough for ten years—how could he be taken!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Congjian had left a hundred thousand elite troops and ten years of grain—how could Zelu be taken!

sentences.zh: 上亦疑之，以問李德裕，對曰：「小小進退，兵家之常。

translations.literal: The emperor also doubted this and questioned Li Deyu, who replied: "Small advances and retreats are the constant of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had doubts too and asked Li Deyu, who answered, "Small gains and setbacks are normal in war.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿聽外議，則成功必矣！」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty not to listen to outside discussion, and then success is certain!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty ignores outside talk, victory is certain!

sentences.zh: 上乃謂宰相曰：「為我語朝士：有上疏沮議者，我必於賊境上斬之！」

translations.literal: The emperor then said to the chief ministers: "Speak for me to the court gentlemen: whoever memorializes to obstruct the plan, I shall behead on the rebel border!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told the chief ministers, "Tell the court for me: anyone who memorializes to obstruct this campaign, I will behead on the rebel border!

sentences.zh: 議者乃止。

translations.literal: The discussants then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The critics fell silent.

sentences.zh: 何弘敬聞王宰將至，恐忠武兵入魏境，軍中有變，蒼黃出師。

translations.literal: When He Hongjing heard Wang Zai was about to arrive, he feared Zhongwu troops would enter Wei territory and that there would be mutiny in the army, and in panic marched out.
translations.idiomatic: When He Hongjing heard Wang Zai was coming, he feared Zhongwu troops entering Weibo might spark a mutiny and hurriedly took the field.

sentences.zh: 丙子，弘敬奏，已自將全軍渡漳水，趣磁州。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Hongjing memorialized that he had personally led the full army across the Zhang River and was hurrying to Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Hongjing reported that he had personally led his full army across the Zhang River toward Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，李德裕上言：「河陽兵力寡弱，自科斗店之敗，賊勢愈熾。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Li Deyu submitted: "Heyang's military strength is few and weak; since the defeat at Kedou Post, the rebels' momentum has grown fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, Li Deyu submitted, "Heyang is weak. Since the defeat at Kedou Post, the rebels have grown bolder.

sentences.zh: 王茂元復有疾，人情危怯，欲退保懷州。

translations.literal: Wang Maoyuan again had illness; men's hearts were fearful and timid, and they wished to withdraw and hold Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyuan was ill again, morale was shaky, and his men wanted to fall back on Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見元和以來諸賊，常視官軍寡弱之處，並力攻之，一軍不支，然後更攻它處。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately seen that since the Yuanhe era the various rebels have commonly looked for places where government armies were few and weak, concentrated their strength to attack them, and when one army could not hold, then attacked elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yuanhe era, rebels have always looked for the weakest government force, concentrated against it, and once that army broke, moved on elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 今魏博未與賊戰，西軍閡險不進，故賊得並力南下。

translations.literal: Now Weibo has not yet fought the rebels, and the western armies are blocked by peril and do not advance, so the rebels can combine their strength and drive south.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo still has not engaged the enemy, and the western armies are stuck in the mountains, so the rebels can mass and push south.

sentences.zh: 若河陽退縮，不惟虧沮軍聲，兼恐震驚洛師。

translations.literal: If Heyang retreats and shrinks back, not only will military reputation be damaged and discouraged, but there is also fear of shocking the capital at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: If Heyang pulls back, it will not only wreck morale but may panic Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 望詔王宰更不之磁州，亟以忠武軍應援河陽；

translations.literal: I hope an edict will order Wang Zai no longer to go to Ci Prefecture, and urgently send the Zhongwu army to reinforce Heyang;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Wang Zai be redirected from Ci Prefecture and that the Zhongwu army be sent at once to reinforce Heyang;

sentences.zh: 不惟扞蔽東都，兼可臨制魏博。

translations.literal: not only shielding the eastern capital, but also able to oversee and control Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: that will shield the eastern capital and also keep Weibo in check.

sentences.zh: 若慮全軍供餉難給，且令發先鋒五千人赴河陽，亦足張聲勢。」

translations.literal: If one fears that supplying the full army would be hard to provide for, then at least order the vanguard of five thousand men sent to Heyang—that too is enough to display force."
translations.idiomatic: If supplying the whole army is too hard, send five thousand vanguard troops to Heyang—that alone would stiffen our position.

sentences.zh: 甲申，又奏請敕王宰以全軍繼進，仍急以器械繒帛助河陽窘乏。

translations.literal: On jiashen, he again memorialized requesting an edict ordering Wang Zai to follow with the full army, and still urgently to send weapons, silks, and cloth to aid Heyang's pressing shortage.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, he submitted again, asking that Wang Zai follow with the full army and that weapons, silks, and cloth be rushed to relieve Heyang's shortages.

sentences.zh: 上皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 王茂元軍萬善，劉稹遣牙將張巨、劉公直等會薛茂卿共攻之，期以九月朔圍萬善。

translations.literal: Wang Maoyuan's army was at Wanshan; Liu Zhen sent military tooth-generals Zhang Ju, Liu Gongzhi, and others to join Xue Maoqing in a joint attack, fixing the first day of the ninth month to invest Wanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyuan held Wanshan. Liu Zhen sent generals Zhang Ju and Liu Gongzhi to join Xue Maoqing in a combined attack, set for the first day of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，公直等潛師先過萬善南五里，焚雍店。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Gongzhi and the others secretly led troops first past five li south of Wanshan and burned Yong Post.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, Gongzhi and the others slipped past Wanshan by five li to the south and burned Yong Post.

sentences.zh: 巨引兵繼之，過萬善，覘知城中守備單弱，欲專有功，遂攻之。

translations.literal: Ju led troops after them, passed Wanshan, reconnoitered and knew the city's defenses were thin and weak, wished to monopolize the merit, and thereupon attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju followed, passed Wanshan, saw how thinly the town was held, wanted the credit for himself, and attacked.

sentences.zh: 日昃，城且拔，乃使人告公直等。

translations.literal: When the sun slanted westward, the city was about to be taken, and only then did he send men to inform Gongzhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the town was nearly taken before he sent word to Gongzhi and the rest.

sentences.zh: 時義成軍適至，茂元困急，欲帥眾棄城走。

translations.literal: At that time the Yicheng army happened to arrive; Maoyuan was pressed in peril and wished to lead the masses, abandon the city, and flee.
translations.idiomatic: The Yicheng army had just arrived. Maoyuan was in desperate straits and wanted to abandon the town and flee.

sentences.zh: 都虞候孟章遮馬諫曰：「賊眾自有前卻，半在雍店，半在此，乃亂兵耳。

translations.literal: Chief Commandant Meng Zhang blocked his horse and remonstrated, saying: "The rebel masses naturally have advance and retreat of their own; half are at Yong Post and half are here—they are a disordered army.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Commandant Meng Zhang seized his bridle and pleaded, "The enemy is split—half at Yong Post, half here. They are a disordered force.

sentences.zh: 今義成軍才至，尚未食，聞僕射走，則自潰矣。

translations.literal: Now the Yicheng army has just arrived and has not yet eaten; if they hear the Vice Commissioner flee, they will collapse of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Yicheng troops have just arrived and have not even eaten. If they hear you run, they will break on their own.

sentences.zh: 願且強留！」

translations.literal: I wish you would force yourself to stay for the time being!"
translations.idiomatic: Please hold your ground!

sentences.zh: 茂元乃止。

translations.literal: Maoyuan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan stayed.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，公直等不至，巨引兵退，始登山，微雨晦黑，自相驚曰：「追兵近矣！」

translations.literal: It happened that night fell; Gongzhi and the others did not arrive, Ju withdrew his troops, and just as they began to climb the mountain, a light rain made the darkness thick, and they startled one another, saying: "Pursuing troops are near!"
translations.idiomatic: Night fell before Gongzhi and the others arrived. Ju pulled back and had just begun to climb the mountain when a drizzle deepened the dark. His men panicked one another, crying, "Pursuers are close!

sentences.zh: 皆走，人馬相踐，墜崖谷死者甚眾。

translations.literal: All fled; men and horses trampled one another, and very many fell into cliffs and ravines and died.
translations.idiomatic: They all fled. Men and horses trampled one another, and a great many plunged off the cliffs and perished in the ravines below.

sentences.zh: 上以王茂元、王宰兩節度使共處河陽非宜，庚寅，李德裕等奏：「茂元習吏事而非將才，請以宰為河陽行營攻討使。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered it unsuitable for the two military governors Wang Maoyuan and Wang Zai to share Heyang together. On gengyin, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "Maoyuan is versed in administrative affairs but is not a general's talent; we request that Zai be made Heyang Forward-Camp Attack and Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged it unwise for two military governors, Wang Maoyuan and Wang Zai, to hold Heyang together. On gengyin, Li Deyu and his colleagues submitted a memorial: "Maoyuan is skilled in administration but lacks the talent of a field commander. We ask that Zai be appointed Heyang Forward-Camp Attack and Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 茂元病癒，止令鎮河陽，病困亦免他虞。」

translations.literal: Maoyuan's illness has healed; he need only be ordered to hold Heyang, and if he falls ill again, that also removes other worries."
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan has recovered from his illness and need only be left to hold Heyang. If he falls ill again, that will spare us other concerns as well.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛卿，以宰兼河陽行營攻討使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinqi, Zai was additionally appointed Heyang Forward-Camp Attack and Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the xinqi cyclical day, Zai was also made Heyang Forward-Camp Attack and Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 何弘敬奏拔肥鄉、平恩，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: He Hongjing reported capturing Feixiang and Ping'en, with very many killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing reported that he had taken Feixiang and Ping'en, with heavy casualties on both sides.

sentences.zh: 得劉稹榜貼，皆謂官軍為賊，雲遇之即須痛殺。

translations.literal: They obtained Liu Zhen's posted proclamations, all calling the government armies bandits and saying that upon meeting them they must be slaughtered without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Among the captured materials were Liu Zhen's posted proclamations, which called the imperial armies bandits and ordered that anyone who encountered them was to kill them without quarter.

sentences.zh: 癸已，上謂宰相：「何弘敬已克兩縣，可釋前疑。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Emperor told the chancellors: "He Hongjing has already captured two counties; earlier suspicions may be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the Emperor told his chancellors, "He Hongjing has already taken two counties. Our earlier doubts about him can be put to rest.

sentences.zh: 既有殺傷，雖欲持兩端，不可得已。」

translations.literal: Since there have already been killings and wounds, even if he wished to play both sides, he cannot do so now."
translations.idiomatic: Now that blood has been shed, even if he wanted to sit on the fence, he no longer can.

sentences.zh: 乃加弘敬檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing was then promoted to acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 丙午，河陽奏王茂元薨。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Heyang reported that Wang Maoyuan had died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Heyang reported the death of Wang Maoyuan.

sentences.zh: 李德裕奏：「王宰止可令以忠武節度使將萬善營兵，不可使兼領河陽，恐其不愛河陽州縣，恣為侵擾，又，河陽節度先領懷州刺史，常以判官攝事，割河南五縣租賦隸河陽，不若遂以五縣置孟州，其懷州別置刺史。

translations.literal: Li Deyu memorialized: "Wang Zai should only be allowed to lead the Wanshan Camp troops as Military Governor of Zhongwu; he must not be permitted to hold Heyang concurrently, for fear that he will not cherish Heyang's prefectures and counties and will wantonly harass them. Moreover, the Heyang military governorship formerly also held the post of Prefect of Huai Prefecture, with a judge often acting in his stead; the five counties of Henan had their tax levies assigned to Heyang. It would be better to establish Meng Prefecture from those five counties and appoint a separate Prefect for Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu submitted a memorial: "Wang Zai should be limited to leading the Wanshan Camp as Military Governor of Zhongwu. He must not also command Heyang, lest he care nothing for Heyang's prefectures and counties and plunder them at will. Furthermore, the Heyang governor had long doubled as Prefect of Huai, with a subordinate judge handling day-to-day affairs, while five Henan counties had their tax revenues assigned to Heyang. It would be better to carve those five counties into a new Meng Prefecture and appoint a separate prefect for Huai.

sentences.zh: 俟昭義平日，仍割澤州隸河陽節度，則太行之險不在昭義，而河陽遂為重鎮，東都無復憂矣！」

translations.literal: When Zhaoyi is pacified, Ze Prefecture should still be assigned to the Heyang military governorship; then the peril of the Taihang Mountains will no longer lie with Zhaoyi, Heyang will become a major stronghold, and the Eastern Capital will have no further cause for worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhaoyi is pacified, Ze Prefecture should be transferred to Heyang as well. Then the Taihang passes will no longer be in rebel hands, Heyang will become a true stronghold, and the Eastern Capital will be secure at last!

sentences.zh: 上采其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以河南尹敬昕為河陽節度、懷孟觀察使，王宰將行營以扞敵，昕供饋餉而已。

translations.literal: On wushen, Jing Xin, Intendant of Henan, was made Military Governor of Heyang and Inspector of Huai and Meng; Wang Zai would lead the forward camp to repel the enemy, while Xin would only supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Jing Xin, Intendant of Henan, was appointed Military Governor of Heyang and Inspector of Huai and Meng. Wang Zai would command the forward camp against the enemy, while Xin would be responsible only for supplying the army.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以石雄代李彥佐為晉絳行營節度使，令自冀氏取潞州，仍分兵屯翼城以備侵軼。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Shi Xiong replaced Li Yanzuo as Jin- and Jiang-Ford Forward-Camp Military Governor, ordered to take Luzhou from Jishi, and to detach troops to garrison Yicheng against raids.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Shi Xiong replaced Li Yanzuo as Military Governor of the Jin- and Jiang-Ford Forward Camp. He was ordered to advance on Luzhou from Jishi and to detach troops to hold Yicheng against enemy raids.

sentences.zh: 是月，吐蕃論恐熱屯大夏川，尚婢婢遣其將厖結心及莽羅薛呂將精兵五萬擊之。

translations.literal: That month, the Tibetan Lun Quren encamped at Daxia River; Shang Pipi sent her generals Pang Jiexin and Mangluo Xuelü to lead fifty thousand elite troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: That month, the Tibetan warlord Lun Quren encamped on the Daxia River. Shang Pipi sent her generals Pang Jiexin and Mangluo Xuelü at the head of fifty thousand elite troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 至河州南，莽羅薛呂伏兵四萬於險阻，厖結心伏萬人於柳林中，以千騎登山，飛矢系書罵之。

translations.literal: When they reached south of He Prefecture, Mangluo Xuelü hid forty thousand troops in difficult terrain, Pang Jiexin hid ten thousand in a willow grove, and with a thousand horsemen climbed the mountain, shooting arrows with letters attached to revile him.
translations.idiomatic: South of He Prefecture, Mangluo Xuelü concealed forty thousand men in rugged ground while Pang Jiexin hid ten thousand in a willow grove. A thousand horsemen then rode up the heights and shot arrows bearing insults tied to their shafts.

sentences.zh: 恐熱怒，將兵數萬追之，厖結心陽敗走，時為馬乏不進之狀。

translations.literal: Quren grew angry and led tens of thousands of troops in pursuit; Pang Jiexin feigned defeat and fled, at times making a show of horses exhausted and unable to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Quren set off in pursuit with tens of thousands of men. Pang Jiexin pretended to flee in defeat, deliberately giving the appearance of horses too weary to keep moving.

sentences.zh: 恐熱追之益急，不覺行數十里，伏兵發，斷其歸路，夾擊之。

translations.literal: Quren pursued ever more urgently, unaware that he had gone several tens of li before the ambush was sprung, his line of retreat cut, and he was struck from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Quren pressed the pursuit harder and harder until, without noticing, he had gone dozens of li. Then the ambush closed in, his retreat was cut off, and he was attacked from both flanks.

sentences.zh: 會大風飛沙，溪谷皆溢，恐熱大敗，伏屍五十里，溺死者不可勝數，恐熱單騎遁歸。

translations.literal: Just then a great wind blew flying sand, streams and ravines all overflowed, Quren suffered a great defeat, corpses lay hidden for fifty li, drowned dead were beyond counting, and Quren fled home alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind whipped up sand and dust, streams and ravines flooded, and Quren's army collapsed in disaster. Dead bodies littered the ground for fifty li, drowned men were beyond counting, and Quren escaped alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 石雄代李彥佐之明日，即引兵逾烏嶺，破五寨，殺獲千計。

translations.literal: The day after Shi Xiong replaced Li Yanzuo, he immediately led troops over Wuling Pass, broke five stockades, and killed and captured men by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The day after replacing Li Yanzuo, Shi Xiong led his men over Wuling Pass, stormed five stockades, and killed or captured thousands.

sentences.zh: 時王宰軍萬善，劉沔軍石會，皆顧望未進。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zai's army was at Wanshan and Liu Mian's army at Shihui; both hesitated and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Zai's army at Wanshan and Liu Mian's at Shihui both hung back and refused to push forward.

sentences.zh: 上得雄捷書，喜甚。

translations.literal: The Emperor received Xiong's report of victory and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor received Xiong's report of victory, he was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚申，臨朝，謂宰相曰：「雄真良將！」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, at court audience he told the chancellors: "Xiong is truly a fine general!"
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, the Emperor held court and told his chancellors, "Xiong is a true commander!

sentences.zh: 李德裕因言：「比年前潞州市有男子磬折唱曰：『石雄七千人至矣！』

translations.literal: Li Deyu then said: "Some years ago in Luzhou city there was a man who bowed deeply and sang, saying: 'Shi Xiong's seven thousand men have arrived!
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu added, "Some years ago in Luzhou city, a man bowed low and sang aloud, 'Shi Xiong's seven thousand men have come!

sentences.zh: 劉從諫以為妖言，斬之。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian considered it demonic talk and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian took this for sorcerous prophecy and had the man executed.

sentences.zh: 破潞州者必雄也。」

translations.literal: The one who will break Luzhou must be Xiong."
translations.idiomatic: The man who will take Luzhou is surely Xiong.

sentences.zh: 詔賜雄帛為優賞，雄悉置軍門，自依士卒例先取一匹，餘悉分將士，故士卒樂為之致死。

translations.literal: An edict awarded Xiong silk cloth as a special reward. Xiong placed it all at the camp gate, took one piece himself according to the soldiers' allotment, and distributed the rest entirely among the officers and men; therefore the troops were glad to fight to the death for him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Xiong a special award of silk. He piled it all at the camp gate, took one bolt for himself on the same terms as an ordinary soldier, and divided the rest among his officers and men. From then on, his troops were eager to die in his service.

sentences.zh: 初，劉沔破回鶻，得太和公主，張仲武疾之，由是有隙；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Mian defeated the Uyghurs and obtained Princess Taihe, Zhang Zhongwu resented this, and from this there arose a rift;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Liu Mian defeated the Uyghurs and recovered Princess Taihe, Zhang Zhongwu resented him, and bad blood grew between them.

sentences.zh: 上使李回至幽州和解之，仲武意終不平。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Li Hui to You Prefecture to reconcile them, but Zhongwu's mind remained unsettled to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Li Hui to You Prefecture to mediate, but Zhongwu's resentment never truly subsided.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐其以私憾敗事，辛未，徙沔為義成節度使，以前荊南節度使李石為河東節度使。

translations.literal: The court feared that private resentment would ruin the campaign; on xinwei, Mian was transferred to be Military Governor of Yicheng, and the former Military Governor of Jingnan, Li Shi, was made Military Governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that private grudges would wreck the campaign, the court on xinwei transferred Mian to Yicheng and appointed the former Jingnan governor Li Shi as Military Governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 党項寇鹽州，以前武寧節度使李彥佐為朔方靈鹽節度使。

translations.literal: The Tangut raided Yan Prefecture; the former Military Governor of Wuning, Li Yanzuo, was made Military Governor of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Yan Prefecture, the former Wuning governor Li Yanzuo was appointed Military Governor of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，邠寧奏党項入寇。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Binning reported Tangut incursions.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Binning reported Tangut raids.

sentences.zh: 李德裕奏：「党項愈熾，不可不為區處。

translations.literal: Li Deyu memorialized: "The Tangut are growing ever fiercer; measures cannot fail to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu submitted a memorial: "The Tangut threat grows fiercer by the day. We cannot leave it unaddressed.

sentences.zh: 聞党項分隸諸鎮，剽掠於此則亡逃歸彼。

translations.literal: I hear that the Tangut are divided among the various commands; when they plunder here they flee and return there.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that the Tangut bands are scattered among the various commands. When they raid one district, they flee into another.

sentences.zh: 節度使各利其駝馬，不為擒送，以此無由禁戢。

translations.literal: Each military governor profits from their camels and horses and does not capture and deliver them; for this reason there is no way to restrain and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Each governor profits from the loot—especially camels and horses—and refuses to arrest and hand over the raiders. That is why the raids cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 臣屢奏不若使一鎮統之，陛下以為一鎮專領党項權太重。

translations.literal: Your servant has repeatedly memorialized that it would be better to have one command govern them all, but Your Majesty considered one command's exclusive control over the Tangut too great a concentration of power.
translations.idiomatic: I have repeatedly urged that a single command be put in charge, but Your Majesty felt that giving one governor sole authority over the Tangut would concentrate too much power.

sentences.zh: 臣今請以皇子兼統諸道，擇中朝廉干之臣為之副，居於夏州，理其辭訟，庶為得宜。」

translations.literal: Your servant now requests that an imperial prince concurrently command the various circuits, with a capable and upright official from the central court chosen as his deputy, residing at Xia Prefecture to handle their lawsuits—then matters may be handled appropriately."
translations.idiomatic: I now propose that an imperial prince be placed in overall command, with a capable and upright official from the capital as his deputy stationed at Xia Prefecture to adjudicate disputes. That, I believe, would be the proper arrangement.

sentences.zh: 乃以兗王岐為靈、夏等六道元帥兼安撫党項大使，又以御史中丞李回為安撫党項副使，史館修撰鄭亞為元帥判官，令繼詔往安撫党項及六鎮百姓。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Yan Qi was made Commander-in-Chief of the six circuits of Ling, Xia, and others and concurrently Grand Commissioner for Pacifying the Tangut; Censor-in-Chief Li Hui was made Deputy Commissioner for Pacifying the Tangut; Historiographer Zheng Ya was made the commander's judge; and they were ordered to proceed to pacify the Tangut and the people of the six commands.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, Prince Qi of Yan was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the six Ling-Xia circuits and Grand Commissioner for Pacifying the Tangut. Censor-in-Chief Li Hui became his deputy, Historiographer Zheng Ya his chief aide, and the three were dispatched to pacify the Tangut and the people of the six frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 安南經略使武渾役將士治城，將士作亂，燒城樓，劫府庫。

translations.literal: The Annam Frontier Commissioner Wu Hun conscripted officers and soldiers to repair the city walls; the troops mutinied, burned the gate towers, and plundered the government storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: In Annam, Frontier Commissioner Wu Hun forced his troops to work on the city walls. They mutinied, burned the gate towers, and looted the government stores.

sentences.zh: 渾奔廣州，監軍段士則撫安亂眾。

translations.literal: Hun fled to Guang Prefecture; the army supervisor Duan Shize pacified the mutinous masses.
translations.idiomatic: Hun fled to Guang Prefecture while army supervisor Duan Shize calmed the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 忠武軍素號精勇，王宰治軍嚴整，昭義人甚憚之。

translations.literal: The Zhongwu army had long been famed for elite courage; Wang Zai governed the army with strict order, and the people of Zhaoyi greatly feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongwu army had long been renowned for its fighting spirit, and Wang Zai ran a tight camp. The people of Zhaoyi feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 薛茂卿以科斗寨之功，意望超遷。

translations.literal: Xue Maoqing, on account of his achievement at Kedou Stockade, hoped for extraordinary promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his victory at Kedou Stockade, Xue Maoqing expected a swift and exceptional promotion.

sentences.zh: 或謂劉稹曰：「留後所求者節耳。

translations.literal: Someone told Liu Zhen: "What the acting governor seeks is only a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Liu Zhen, "All the acting governor wants is a commission of his own.

sentences.zh: 茂卿太深入，多殺官軍，激怒朝廷，此節所以來益遲也。」

translations.literal: Maoqing pressed too deep, killed too many government troops, and enraged the court—that is why the commission has come ever more slowly."
translations.idiomatic: But Maoqing pushed too far, killed too many imperial troops, and enraged the court. That is why the commission keeps being delayed.

sentences.zh: 由是無賞。

translations.literal: For this reason there was no reward.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason, no reward was given.

sentences.zh: 茂卿溫懟，密與王宰通謀。

translations.literal: Maoqing simmered with resentment and secretly entered into collusion with Wang Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with resentment, Maoqing secretly opened negotiations with Wang Zai.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁巳，宰引兵攻天井關，茂卿小戰，遽引兵走，宰遂克天井關守之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingsi, Zai led troops to attack Tianjing Pass; Maoqing fought briefly, then abruptly withdrew his troops and fled; Zai thereupon captured Tianjing Pass and held it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingsi, Zai attacked Tianjing Pass. Maoqing offered only a brief resistance, then pulled back. Zai took the pass and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 關東西寨聞茂卿不守，皆退走，宰遂焚大小箕村。

translations.literal: The stockades east and west of the pass, hearing that Maoqing would not hold, all withdrew and fled; Zai then burned the villages of Daji and Xiaoji.
translations.idiomatic: When the stockades east and west of the pass learned that Maoqing would not stand firm, they all abandoned their positions. Zai then burned the villages of Daji and Xiaoji.

sentences.zh: 茂卿入澤州，密使諜召宰進攻澤州，當為內應。

translations.literal: Maoqing entered Ze Prefecture and secretly sent a spy to summon Zai to attack Ze Prefecture, saying he would act as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqing withdrew into Ze Prefecture and secretly sent a spy urging Zai to attack the city, promising to serve as his inside ally.

sentences.zh: 宰疑，不敢進，失期不至，茂卿拊膺頓足而已。

translations.literal: Zai was suspicious and did not dare advance; missing the appointed time, he did not arrive; Maoqing could only beat his breast and stamp his feet.
translations.idiomatic: Zai hesitated and would not advance. He missed the agreed time, and Maoqing could only wring his hands in frustration.

sentences.zh: 稹知之，誘茂卿至潞州，殺之，並其族，以兵馬使劉公直代茂卿，安全慶守烏嶺，李佐堯守雕黃嶺，郭僚守石會，康良佺守武鄉。

translations.literal: When Zhen learned of it, he lured Maoqing to Luzhou, killed him, and exterminated his clan; he replaced Maoqing with Cavalry Commissioner Liu Gongzhi, put An Qingqing to hold Wuling Pass, Li Zuoyao to hold Diaohuang Ridge, Guo Liao to hold Shihui, and Kang Liangquan to hold Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen learned of the plot, he lured Maoqing to Luzhou, killed him, and wiped out his clan. He replaced Maoqing with Cavalry Commissioner Liu Gongzhi, posted An Qingqing at Wuling Pass, Li Zuoyao at Diaohuang Ridge, Guo Liao at Shihui, and Kang Liangquan at Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 僚，誼之侄也。

translations.literal: Liao was the nephew of Guo Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Liao was a nephew of Guo Yi.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，王宰進攻澤州，與劉公直戰，不利，公直乘勝復天井關。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Wang Zai advanced to attack Ze Prefecture and fought Liu Gongzhi, with an unfavorable outcome; Gongzhi pressed his victory and recaptured Tianjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Wang Zai attacked Ze Prefecture and fought Liu Gongzhi without success. Gongzhi pressed his advantage and retook Tianjing Pass.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，宰進擊公直，大破之，遂圍陵川，克之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Zai advanced to strike Gongzhi and routed him greatly, then besieged Lingchuan and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Zai attacked Gongzhi again and routed him, then besieged and captured Lingchuan.

sentences.zh: 河東奏克石會關。

translations.literal: Hedong reported capturing Shihui Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong reported the capture of Shihui Pass.

sentences.zh: 洺州刺史李恬，石之從兄也。

translations.literal: Li Tian, Prefect of Ming Prefecture, was Li Shi's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tian, Prefect of Ming, was Li Shi's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 石至太原，劉稹遣軍將賈群詣石，以恬書與石云：「稹願舉族歸命相公，奉從諫喪歸葬東都。」

translations.literal: When Shi reached Taiyuan, Liu Zhen sent the army officer Jia Qun to Shi, with a letter from Tian to Shi saying: "Zhen wishes to surrender his entire clan to the Commissioner, and to send Congjian's coffin back for burial in the Eastern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shi reached Taiyuan, Liu Zhen sent the officer Jia Qun with a letter from Li Tian. It read, "Zhen is willing to surrender his whole clan to you, Commissioner, and to send Congjian's coffin home for burial in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 石囚群，以其書聞。

translations.literal: Shi imprisoned Qun and reported the letter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi imprisoned Jia Qun and forwarded the letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 李德裕上言：「今官軍四合，捷書日至，賊勢窮蹙，故偽輸誠款，翼以緩師，稍得自完，復來侵軼。

translations.literal: Li Deyu submitted: "Now the government armies converge from four directions, reports of victory arrive daily, and the rebels' strength is cornered; therefore they falsely offer sincere submission, hoping to slow the army, recover themselves somewhat, and again come raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu advised the throne: "The imperial armies now close in from every side and victory reports arrive daily. The rebels are desperate, and this supposed offer of surrender is a sham meant to slow our advance. Once they recover, they will raid again.

sentences.zh: 望詔石答恬書云：『前書未敢聞奏。

translations.literal: I hope an edict will order Shi to reply to Tian's letter, saying: 'The previous letter I did not dare report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Shi be instructed to answer Li Tian's letter as follows: 'I did not dare report your earlier letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 若郎君誠能悔過，舉族面縛，待罪境上，則石當親往受降，護送歸闕。

translations.literal: If the young lord can truly repent his faults, bind his whole clan with faces bound, and await judgment at the border, then Shi will personally go to accept surrender and escort him back to court.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly repent and come forward with your whole clan in bonds to await judgment at the frontier, I will go in person to accept your surrender and escort you to the capital.

sentences.zh: 若虛為誠款，先求解兵，次望洗雪，則石必不敢以百口保人。』

translations.literal: If this is a false show of sincerity, first seeking to have the army stand down and then hoping to be cleared of guilt, then Shi absolutely dare not guarantee a man's life with the lives of his hundred kin.'
translations.idiomatic: But if this is a false show of loyalty—first asking us to halt the campaign, then hoping to be cleared of guilt—I cannot stake the lives of my entire household on your word.

sentences.zh: 仍望招諸道，乘其上下離心，速進兵攻討，不過旬朔，必內自生變。」

translations.literal: I further hope that the various circuits will be summoned, seizing the moment when superiors and subordinates are divided in heart, to advance troops quickly in attack and pacification; within no more than ten days or a month, rebellion will surely arise within them."
translations.idiomatic: I also urge that all circuits be ordered to press the attack while the rebels are divided within. If we move quickly, within ten days or a month they will turn on one another.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺崔碣上疏請受其降，上怒，貶碣鄧城令。

translations.literal: Right Reminder Cui Jie submitted a memorial requesting that the surrender be accepted; the Emperor grew angry and demoted Jie to Magistrate of Dengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Right Reminder Cui Jie memorialized the throne urging acceptance of the surrender. The Emperor was furious and demoted him to magistrate of Dengcheng.

sentences.zh: 初，劉沔破回鶻，留兵三千戍橫水柵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Mian defeated the Uyghurs, he left three thousand troops to garrison Hengshui Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Liu Mian defeated the Uyghurs, he had left three thousand men to garrison Hengshui Stockade.

sentences.zh: 河東行營都知兵馬使王逢奏乞益榆社兵，詔河東以兵二千赴之。

translations.literal: Wang Feng, Hedong Forward-Camp Director of Military Affairs, memorialized requesting reinforcements for Yushe; an edict ordered Hedong to send two thousand troops there.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng, Hedong Forward-Camp Director of Military Affairs, asked for reinforcements at Yushe. An edict ordered Hedong to dispatch two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時河東無兵，守倉庫者及工匠皆出從軍，李石召橫水戍卒千五百人，使都將楊弁將之詣逢，壬午，戍卒至太原。

translations.literal: At that time Hedong had no troops; those guarding the storehouses and the artisans all went out to join the army. Li Shi summoned fifteen hundred garrison soldiers from Hengshui and had Commandant Yang Bian lead them to Feng; on renwu, the garrison soldiers reached Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong had no spare troops. Even warehouse guards and artisans were sent to the front. Li Shi called up fifteen hundred men from the Hengshui garrison and put Commandant Yang Bian in charge of escorting them to Wang Feng. On renwu they reached Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，軍士出征，人給絹二匹。

translations.literal: Earlier, when soldiers went on campaign, each man was given two bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, each soldier sent on campaign had been given two bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 劉沔之去，竭府庫自隨，石初至，軍用乏，以己絹益之，人才得一匹。

translations.literal: When Liu Mian departed, he exhausted the treasury and took it with him; when Shi first arrived, military supplies were scarce, and he supplemented them with his own silk, so each man received only one bolt.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Mian left, he had drained the treasury and taken everything with him. Li Shi had just arrived to find the coffers empty. He added silk from his own funds, but each man received only one bolt.

sentences.zh: 時已歲盡，軍士求過正旦而行，監軍呂義忠累牒趣之。

translations.literal: The year was already ending; the soldiers asked to wait until after New Year's Day before departing, but the army supervisor Lü Yizhong repeatedly sent dispatches urging them on.
translations.idiomatic: The year was nearly over, and the men asked to wait until after New Year's Day before marching. Army supervisor Lü Yizhong sent dispatch after dispatch ordering them to move at once.

sentences.zh: 楊弁因眾心之怒，又知城中空虛，遂作亂。

translations.literal: Yang Bian, taking advantage of the troops' anger and knowing also that the city was empty, thereupon raised a mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bian seized on the men's anger, and knowing the city was nearly undefended, he led a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 武宗至道昭肅孝皇帝中會昌四年（

translations.literal: Middle reign of Emperor Wuzong, the Filial Emperor of Supreme Way and Solemn Clarity, fourth year of Huichang (
translations.idiomatic: Middle reign of Emperor Wuzong, the Filial Emperor of Supreme Way and Solemn Clarity, fourth year of Huichang (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元八四四年）

translations.literal: jiazi, corresponding to 844 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi, corresponding to 844 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉朔，楊弁帥其眾剽掠城市，殺都頭梁季葉，李石奔汾州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yiyou, the first day of the month, Yang Bian led his masses in plundering the city, killed Commandant Liang Jiye, and Li Shi fled to Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the first day, yiyou, Yang Bian led his men in looting the city, killed Commandant Liang Jiye, and Li Shi fled to Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弁據軍府，釋賈群之囚，使其侄與之俱詣劉稹，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Bian seized the military headquarters, released the prisoner Jia Qun, and had his nephew go with him to Liu Zhen to become sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Bian seized the military headquarters, freed Jia Qun from prison, and sent his nephew with Jia to Liu Zhen to swear brotherhood with him.

sentences.zh: 稹大喜。

translations.literal: Zhen was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 石會關守將楊珍聞太原亂，復以關降於稹。

translations.literal: Yang Zhen, the defending general of Shihui Pass, hearing of the turmoil in Taiyuan, again surrendered the pass to Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zhen, commander of Shihui Pass, heard of the uprising in Taiyuan, he surrendered the pass to Zhen once more.

sentences.zh: 戊子，呂義忠遣使言狀，朝議喧然。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Lü Yizhong sent a messenger to report the situation, and court discussion erupted in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Lü Yizhong sent a messenger with a report of the disaster, and the court erupted in alarmed debate.

sentences.zh: 或言兩地皆應罷兵，王宰又上言：「游弈將得劉稹表，臣近遣人至澤潞，賊有意歸附。

translations.literal: Some said both regions should halt the armies; Wang Zai also submitted: "The patrol officer received Liu Zhen's memorial; your servant recently sent men to Ze and Lu, and the rebels intend to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that both fronts should stand down. Wang Zai also submitted a memorial: "A patrol officer has received a petition from Liu Zhen. I recently sent men into Ze and Lu, and the rebels seem willing to submit.

sentences.zh: 若許招納，乞降詔命！」

translations.literal: If acceptance of their submission is permitted, I beg that an edict be issued!"
translations.idiomatic: If their surrender may be accepted, I beg Your Majesty to issue an edict!

sentences.zh: 李德裕上言：「宰擅受稹表，遣人入賊中，曾不聞奏，觀宰意似欲擅招撫之功。

translations.literal: Li Deyu submitted: "Zai accepted Zhen's memorial on his own authority, sent men into the rebel camp, and never reported it to the throne; viewing Zai's intent, he seems to wish to monopolize the credit for accepting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu countered: "Zai accepted Zhen's petition on his own authority, sent men into rebel territory, and never reported it. He plainly wants to claim the credit for accepting their surrender himself.

sentences.zh: 昔韓信破田榮，李靖擒頡利，皆因其請降，潛兵掩襲。

translations.literal: In the past Han Xin broke Tian Rong, and Li Jing captured Jieli—both by using their request for surrender as cover for secretly sending troops in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, Han Xin destroyed Tian Rong and Li Jing captured Jieli Khan by pretending to accept surrender while secretly launching a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 止可令王宰失信，豈得損朝廷威命！

translations.literal: One may only let Wang Zai break faith; how can the court's authority and command be diminished!
translations.idiomatic: We may let Wang Zai break his word if we must, but we cannot let the authority of the throne be diminished!

sentences.zh: 建立奇功，實在今日，必不可以太原小擾，失此事機。

translations.literal: To establish extraordinary achievement is truly a matter for this very day; one absolutely cannot, because of a small disturbance at Taiyuan, lose this opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: The moment to win a decisive victory is now. We must not throw it away over a minor disturbance at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 望即遣供奉官至行營，督其進兵，掩其無備，必須劉稹與諸將皆舉族面縛，方可受納。

translations.literal: I hope that palace attendants will immediately be sent to the forward camps to supervise the advance of troops and strike them unprepared; Liu Zhen and all his generals must bind their entire clans with faces bound before surrender can be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Send palace envoys at once to the forward camps to press the attack and strike while the enemy is off guard. Liu Zhen and his generals must come forward with their entire clans in bonds before we accept any surrender.

sentences.zh: 兼遣供奉官至晉絳行營，密諭石雄以王宰若納劉稹，則雄無功可紀。

translations.literal: At the same time send palace attendants to the Jin- and Jiang-Ford Forward Camp to secretly instruct Shi Xiong that if Wang Zai accepts Liu Zhen, then Xiong will have no achievement to record.
translations.idiomatic: Also send a palace envoy to the Jin- and Jiang-Ford Forward Camp with a secret message for Shi Xiong: if Wang Zai accepts Liu Zhen's surrender, Xiong will have no glory left to win.

sentences.zh: 雄於垂成之際，須自取奇功，勿失此便。」

translations.literal: Xiong, at the moment when success is near, must seize extraordinary achievement for himself—do not lose this opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: Victory is within reach. Xiong must seize a decisive triumph for himself now and not let this chance slip away.

sentences.zh: 又為相府與宰書，言：「昔王承宗雖逆命，猶遣弟承恭奉表詣張相祈哀，又遣其子知感、知信入朝，憲宗猶未之許。

translations.literal: He also wrote a letter from the chancellery to Zai, saying: "In the past, although Wang Chengzong defied the command, he still sent his younger brother Chenggong to present a memorial to Chancellor Zhang to plead for mercy, and also sent his sons Zhigan and Zhixin to court—yet Emperor Xianzong still did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a letter from the chancellery to Zai: "Even when Wang Chengzong rebelled, he sent his brother Chenggong with a memorial pleading to Chancellor Zhang, and sent his sons Zhigan and Zhixin to court—and Emperor Xianzong still refused to accept their submission.

sentences.zh: 今劉稹不詣尚書面縛，又不遣血屬祈哀，置章表於衢路之間，游弈將不即毀除，實恐非是。

translations.literal: Now Liu Zhen does not come to the Secretariat with his face bound, nor does he send blood kin to plead for mercy; he places memorials in the public roads, and the patrol officer does not immediately destroy them—this truly seems improper.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen has not come to the Secretariat in bonds, nor sent close kin to plead for mercy. He simply leaves petitions in the public roads, and your patrol officer has not even destroyed them. This is hardly a genuine surrender.

sentences.zh: 況稹與楊弁通姦，逆狀如此，而將帥大臣容受其詐，是私惠歸於臣下，不赦在於朝廷，事體之間，交恐不可。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhen is in league with Yang Bian; his rebellious conduct is such, yet generals and great ministers would tolerate his fraud—then private favor would fall to subordinates while pardon remained with the court; in the matter as a whole, I fear this would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, Zhen is in league with Yang Bian. His rebellion is flagrant, yet a field commander would accept this fraud. That would put private favor in the hands of a subordinate while mercy remained the court's alone. Such an arrangement is intolerable.

sentences.zh: 自今更有章表，宣即所在焚之。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever there are further memorials, order that they be burned on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, any further petitions are to be burned wherever they are found.

sentences.zh: 惟面縛而來，始可容受。」

translations.literal: Only if they come with faces bound may they be accepted."
translations.idiomatic: Only if they come forward in bonds will we accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 德裕又上言：「太原人心從來忠順，止是貧虛，賞犒不足。

translations.literal: Deyu also submitted: "The hearts of the people of Taiyuan have always been loyal and obedient; it is only that they are poor and depleted, and rewards and bonuses were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu added another memorial: "The people of Taiyuan have always been loyal. They rebelled only because they were impoverished and poorly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 況千五百人何能為事！

translations.literal: Moreover, what can fifteen hundred men accomplish!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what can fifteen hundred men really accomplish!

sentences.zh: 必不可姑息寬縱。

translations.literal: One absolutely cannot indulge and leniently release them.
translations.idiomatic: We must not show them leniency.

sentences.zh: 且用兵未罷，深慮所在動心。

translations.literal: Moreover, the use of troops has not yet ceased; I deeply fear that everywhere hearts will be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign is not yet over, and I greatly fear that unrest elsewhere will be stirred up.

sentences.zh: 頃張延賞為張朏出所逐，逃奔漢州，還入成都。

translations.literal: Recently Zhang Yanshang was driven out by Zhang Fei, fled to Han Prefecture, and returned into Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, Zhang Yanshang was driven out by Zhang Fei, fled to Han Prefecture, and then returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 望詔李石、義忠還赴太原行營，召旁近之兵討除亂者。」

translations.literal: I hope an edict will order Li Shi and Yizhong to return to the Taiyuan forward camp and summon nearby troops to suppress and eliminate the mutineers.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Li Shi and Lü Yizhong be ordered back to the Taiyuan forward camp and that nearby troops be summoned to crush the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 上皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every point.

sentences.zh: 是時，李石已至晉州，詔復還太原。

translations.literal: At that time Li Shi had already reached Jin Prefecture; an edict ordered him to return again to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Shi had already reached Jin Prefecture, but an edict ordered him to turn back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，詔王逢悉留太原兵守榆社，以易定千騎、宣武兗海步兵三千討楊弁；

translations.literal: On xinmao, an edict ordered Wang Feng to leave all Taiyuan troops to defend Yushe, and to use one thousand horsemen from Yiding and three thousand infantry from Xuanwu and Yanhai to campaign against Yang Bian;
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao, Wang Feng was ordered to leave every Taiyuan soldier at Yushe and to take one thousand Yiding cavalry plus three thousand Xuanwu and Yanhai infantry against Yang Bian;

sentences.zh: 又詔王元逵以步騎五千自土門入，應接逢軍。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Wang Yuankui to enter through Tumen with five thousand infantry and cavalry to support Feng's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui was also ordered to enter through Tumen with five thousand infantry and cavalry to reinforce Feng's force.

sentences.zh: 忻州刺史李丕奏：「楊弁遣人來為遊說，臣已斬之，兼斷其北出之路，發兵討之。」

translations.literal: Li Pi, prefect of Xin Prefecture, memorialized: "Yang Bian sent men to win me over; I have already executed them, blocked his route northward as well, and raised troops to attack him."
translations.idiomatic: Li Pi, prefect of Xin, reported, "Yang Bian sent envoys to win me over. I have executed them, cut off his escape route to the north, and raised troops to attack him."

sentences.zh: 辛丑，上與宰相議太原事，李德裕曰：「今太原兵皆在外，為亂者止千餘人，諸州鎮必無應者。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the emperor discussed the Taiyuan affair with the chief ministers. Li Deyu said: "Now all Taiyuan's troops are outside; those raising the revolt number only a little over a thousand, and the various prefectures and garrisons will certainly not respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the emperor met with his chief ministers on Taiyuan. Li Deyu said, "Taiyuan's regular troops are all away. The mutineers number barely a thousand, and no other prefecture or garrison will rally to them.

sentences.zh: 計不日誅翦，惟應速詔王逢進軍，至城下必自有變。」

translations.literal: I reckon they can be destroyed within days; we need only quickly order Wang Feng to advance—once he reaches the walls, change will come of itself."
translations.idiomatic: They can be crushed within days. We need only order Wang Feng to march at once; once he reaches the city walls, the situation will turn of its own accord."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「仲武見鎮、魏討澤潞有功，必有慕羨之心，使之討太原何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhongwu saw that Zhen and Wei achieved merit in campaigning against Zelu, so he must feel envy; how would it be to have him campaign against Taiyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhongwu watched Zhen and Wei win glory against Zelu and must envy them. What if we sent him against Taiyuan?"

sentences.zh: 德裕對曰：「鎮州趣太原路最便近。

translations.literal: Deyu replied: "The route from Zhen Prefecture to Taiyuan is the quickest and nearest.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu replied, "The road from Zhen Prefecture to Taiyuan is the shortest and easiest.

sentences.zh: 仲武去年討回鶻，與太原爭功，恐其不戢士卒，平人受害。」

translations.literal: Last year, when Zhongwu campaigned against the Uyghurs, he contended with Taiyuan for credit; I fear he will not restrain his soldiers, and common people will suffer."
translations.idiomatic: Last year, when Zhongwu fought the Uyghurs, he quarreled with Taiyuan over credit for the victory. I fear he will not restrain his men, and civilians will pay the price."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The idea was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使馬元實至太原，曉諭亂兵，且覘其強弱。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the palace attendant Ma Yuanshi to Taiyuan to exhort the mutineers and also to reconnoiter their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the palace envoy Ma Yuanshi to Taiyuan to reason with the mutineers and scout their strength.

sentences.zh: 陳弁與之酣飲三日，且賂之。

translations.literal: Yang Bian drank merrily with him for three days and also bribed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bian wined and dined him for three days straight and bribed him as well.

sentences.zh: 戊申，元實自太原還，上遣詣宰相議之，元實於眾中大言：「相公須早與之節！」

translations.literal: On wushen, Yuanshi returned from Taiyuan. The emperor sent him to confer with the chief ministers. In the assembly Yuanshi spoke loudly: "Your Excellencies must grant him a commission at once!"
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Yuanshi returned from Taiyuan. The emperor sent him to consult the chief ministers, and Yuanshi declared before them all, "Your Excellencies must grant him a commission immediately!"

sentences.zh: 李德裕曰：「何故？」

translations.literal: Li Deyu said: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu asked, "Why?"

sentences.zh: 元實曰：「自牙門至柳子列十五里曳地光明甲，若之何取之！」

translations.literal: Yuanshi said: "From the yamen gate to Liuzi, armor gleaming and dragging on the ground lined the road for fifteen li—how could you take them!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi said, "From the yamen gate to Liuzi, polished armor gleaming in the sun stretched for fifteen li along the road. How could you ever overcome them!"

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「李相正以太原無兵，故發橫水兵赴榆社。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Vice Director Li, because Taiyuan has no troops, sent the Hengshui garrison to Yushe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "Vice Director Li sent the Hengshui garrison to Yushe precisely because Taiyuan had no troops left.

sentences.zh: 庫中之甲盡在行營，弁何能遽致如此之眾乎？」

translations.literal: All the armor in the storehouses is at the forward camp—how could Bian suddenly muster so many?"
translations.idiomatic: Every suit of armor in the arsenal is with the field army. How could Bian suddenly produce a force that size?"

sentences.zh: 元實曰：「太原人勁悍，皆可為兵，弁召募所致耳。」

translations.literal: Yuanshi said: "Taiyuan men are fierce and hardy; all can serve as soldiers. Bian simply recruited them."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi said, "The people of Taiyuan are tough and warlike. Bian simply recruited them—that is all."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「召募須有貨財，李相止以欠軍士絹一匹，無從可得，故致此亂，弁何從得之？」

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Recruitment requires funds and goods. Vice Director Li owed each soldier only one bolt of silk and had no way to obtain it—that is what caused this mutiny. Where could Bian get the means?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "Recruitment takes money and supplies. Vice Director Li owed each man a single bolt of silk and had no way to pay even that—that is what sparked this mutiny. Where would Bian get the funds?"

sentences.zh: 元實辭屈。

translations.literal: Yuanshi was silenced.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi had no reply.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「從其有十五里光明甲，必須殺此賊！」

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Even if they truly have armor gleaming for fifteen li, we must kill this bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "Even if they truly had armor gleaming for fifteen li, we must kill this rebel!"

sentences.zh: 因奏稱：「楊弁微賊，決不可恕。

translations.literal: He then submitted: "Yang Bian is a petty rebel and absolutely cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized, "Yang Bian is a petty rebel and must on no account be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 如國力不及，寧捨劉稹。」

translations.literal: If our national strength falls short, better to abandon Liu Zhen."
translations.idiomatic: If our strength is not equal to both tasks, better to let Liu Zhen go."

sentences.zh: 河東兵戍榆社者聞朝廷令客軍取太原，恐妻孥為所屠滅，乃擁監軍呂義忠自取太原。

translations.literal: The Hedong troops garrisoning Yushe heard that the court had ordered outside armies to take Taiyuan. Fearing their wives and children would be slaughtered, they rallied around the army supervisor Lü Yizhong and took Taiyuan themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong garrison at Yushe heard that the court had ordered outside armies to seize Taiyuan. Fearing their families would be massacred, they rallied around army supervisor Lü Yizhong and retook the city themselves.

sentences.zh: 壬子，克之，生擒楊弁，盡誅亂卒。

translations.literal: On renzi they captured it, took Yang Bian alive, and executed all the mutineers.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi they took the city, captured Yang Bian alive, and executed every mutineer.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day, jiayin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day of the month, jiayin, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，呂義忠奏克太原。

translations.literal: On yimao, Lü Yizhong memorialized that Taiyuan had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Lü Yizhong reported the capture of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，李德裕言於上曰：「王宰久應取澤州，今已遷延兩月。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Li Deyu said to the emperor: "Wang Zai should long ago have taken Ze Prefecture, yet two months have already passed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Li Deyu told the emperor, "Wang Zai should have taken Ze Prefecture long ago, yet two months have already slipped by.

sentences.zh: 蓋宰與石雄素不葉，今得澤州，距上黨猶二百里；

translations.literal: This is because Zai and Shi Xiong have never gotten along. If he now takes Ze Prefecture, Shangdang is still two hundred li away;
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that Zai and Shi Xiong have never been on good terms. Even if he took Ze Prefecture now, Shangdang would still lie two hundred li ahead;

sentences.zh: 而石雄所屯距上黨才百五十里。

translations.literal: yet where Shi Xiong is encamped is only one hundred fifty li from Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Shi Xiong's camp is only one hundred fifty li from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 宰恐攻澤州綴昭義大軍，而雄得乘虛入上黨獨有其功耳。

translations.literal: Zai fears that if he attacks Ze Prefecture he will tie down the Zhaoyi main army, while Xiong will seize the opening to enter Shangdang alone and claim all the glory.
translations.idiomatic: Zai fears that attacking Ze Prefecture will pin down the main Zhaoyi army, while Xiong slips in to take Shangdang alone and win all the glory.

sentences.zh: 又宰生子晏實，其父智興愛而子之，晏實今為磁州刺史，為劉稹所質。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zai raised Yan Shi as a son; his father Zhi Xing loved him as his own. Yan Shi now serves as prefect of Ci Prefecture and is being held hostage by Liu Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Zai had raised Yan Shi as a son—Zhi Xing loved the boy as his own—and Yan Shi now serves as prefect of Ci while Liu Zhen holds him hostage.

sentences.zh: 宰之顧望不敢進，或為此也。」

translations.literal: Zai's hesitation and failure to advance may be for this reason."
translations.idiomatic: Zai's hesitation to advance may stem from this."

sentences.zh: 上命德裕草詔賜宰，督其進兵。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Deyu to draft an edict for Zai, urging him to advance his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Deyu to draft an edict for Wang Zai pressing him to march.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「朕顧茲小寇，終不貸刑。

translations.literal: And he said: "This petty rebel I have in sight—I will never spare him punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "This petty rebel is within my sight, and I will never spare him punishment.

sentences.zh: 亦知晏實是卿愛弟，將申大義，在抑私懷。」

translations.literal: I also know that Yan Shi is your beloved brother. You must uphold the greater principle and set private feeling aside."
translations.idiomatic: I know Yan Shi is your beloved brother, but you must uphold the greater duty and set private feeling aside."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以李石為太子少傅、分司，以河中節度使崔元式為河東節度使，石雄為河中節度使。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Li Shi was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with a sinecure post; Cui Yuanshi, military commissioner of Hezhong, was made military commissioner of Hedong; and Shi Xiong was made military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Li Shi was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with a nominal post at court; Cui Yuanshi, military commissioner of Hezhong, was transferred to Hedong; and Shi Xiong was made military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 元式，元略之弟也。

translations.literal: Yuanshi was the younger brother of Yuanlue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi was the younger brother of Yuanlue.

sentences.zh: 乙未，石雄拔良馬等三寨一堡。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Shi Xiong captured three stockades and one fort at Liangma and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Shi Xiong stormed three stockades and one fort, including Liangma.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，太原獻楊弁及其黨五十四人，皆斬於狗脊嶺。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Taiyuan presented Yang Bian and fifty-four of his followers; all were executed at Goujiling.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Taiyuan sent Yang Bian and fifty-four of his accomplices to the capital; all were beheaded at Goujiling.

sentences.zh: 壬申，李德裕言於上曰：「事固有激發而成功者：陛下命王宰趣磁州，而何弘敬出師；

translations.literal: On renshen, Li Deyu said to the emperor: "Some affairs succeed precisely because they are provoked into motion: Your Majesty ordered Wang Zai to hurry toward Ci Prefecture, and He Hongjing marched out his army;
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Li Deyu told the emperor, "Some campaigns succeed only because one move provokes another: when Your Majesty ordered Wang Zai toward Ci Prefecture, He Hongjing marched out his army;

sentences.zh: 遣客軍討太原，而戍兵先取楊弁。

translations.literal: you sent outside armies against Taiyuan, and the garrison troops took Yang Bian first.
translations.idiomatic: when you sent outside armies against Taiyuan, the garrison troops captured Yang Bian first.

sentences.zh: 今王宰久不進軍，請徙劉沔鎮河陽，仍令以義成精兵二千直抵萬善，處宰肘腋之下。

translations.literal: Now Wang Zai has long failed to advance. I ask that Liu Mian be transferred to garrison Heyang, and that he be ordered to take two thousand elite troops from Yicheng straight to Wanshan, placing him at Zai's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai has stalled for too long. I ask that Liu Mian be posted to Heyang and ordered to take two thousand elite Yicheng troops straight to Wanshan, placing a force at Zai's flank.

sentences.zh: 若宰識朝廷此意，必不敢淹留。

translations.literal: If Zai understands the court's intent, he will surely not dare delay.
translations.idiomatic: If Zai reads the court's intent, he will not dare linger.

sentences.zh: 若宰進軍，沔以重兵在南，聲勢亦壯。」

translations.literal: If Zai advances, Mian with heavy troops to the south will also make the show of force formidable."
translations.idiomatic: If Zai does advance, Mian's heavy force to the south will strengthen the overall position.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以義成節度使劉沔為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Liu Mian, military commissioner of Yicheng, was made military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Liu Mian, military commissioner of Yicheng, was made military commissioner of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 王逢擊昭義將康良佺，敗之。

translations.literal: Wang Feng attacked the Zhaoyi general Kang Liangquan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng attacked the Zhaoyi general Kang Liangquan and routed him.

sentences.zh: 良佺棄石會關，退屯鼓腰嶺。

translations.literal: Liangquan abandoned Shihui Pass and withdrew to encamp at Guyaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Liangquan abandoned Shihui Pass and fell back to Guyaoling.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯遣將軍諦德伊斯難珠等入貢，言欲徙居回鶻牙帳，請發兵之期，集會之地。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz sent Generals Dide Yisinanzhu and others to pay tribute, stating they wished to move to the former Uyghur royal encampment and requesting the date for dispatching troops and the place of assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The Kirghiz sent Generals Dide Yisinanzhu and others to court with tribute, saying they wished to move into the former Uyghur royal encampment and asking when Tang would send troops and where they should rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 上賜詔，諭以「今秋可汗擊回鶻、黑車子之時，當令幽州、太原、振武、天德四鎮出兵要路，邀其亡逸，便申冊命，並依回鶻故事。」

translations.literal: The emperor granted an edict instructing them: "When the khan campaigns against the Uyghurs and the Heichezi this autumn, Youzhou, Taiyuan, Zhenwu, and Tiande should send troops to hold the key passes and intercept any who flee. Investiture will then be conferred, all according to Uyghur precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied by edict that when the khan attacked the Uyghurs and Heichezi that autumn, Youzhou, Taiyuan, Zhenwu, and Tiande should send troops to hold the key routes and cut off fugitives; formal investiture would then follow, on the Uyghur model.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以回鶻衰微，吐蕃內亂，議復河、湟四鎮十八州。

translations.literal: The court, because the Uyghurs were declining and Tibet was torn by internal strife, debated recovering the four garrisons and eighteen prefectures of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: With the Uyghurs in decline and Tibet convulsed by civil war, the court debated recovering the four garrisons and eighteen prefectures of the Hexi region.

sentences.zh: 乃以給事中劉水蒙為巡邊使，使之先備器械糗糧及詗吐蕃守兵眾寡。

translations.literal: Liu Shuimeng, Supervising Secretary, was appointed Frontier Inspector to prepare weapons, provisions, and grain in advance, and to spy out the strength of Tibetan garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shuimeng, a supervising secretary, was made frontier inspector to stock weapons and provisions and to scout the size of Tibetan garrisons.

sentences.zh: 又令天德、振武、河東訓卒礪兵，以俟今秋黠越斯擊回鶻，邀其潰敗之眾南來者，皆委水蒙與節度團練使詳議以聞。

translations.literal: Tiande, Zhenwu, and Hedong were also ordered to drill soldiers and sharpen weapons, awaiting the Kirghiz attack on the Uyghurs this autumn, to intercept fleeing masses coming south—all to be discussed in detail by Shuimeng and the military commissioners and reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande, Zhenwu, and Hedong were also ordered to drill troops and sharpen weapons against the day the Kirghiz struck the Uyghurs that autumn and routed fugitives fled south. Shuimeng and the military commissioners were to work out the details and report back.

sentences.zh: 水蒙，晏之孫也。

translations.literal: Shuimeng was the grandson of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuimeng was a grandson of Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 以道士趙歸真為右街道門教授先生。

translations.literal: The Daoist Zhao Guizhen was made Professor and Master of the Right Street Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Zhao Guizhen was appointed Professor and Master of the Right Street Gate.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃論恐熱之將岌藏豐贊惡恐熱殘忍，降於尚婢婢。

translations.literal: The Tibetan general Jizang Fengzan under Lun Qiner, loathing Qiner's cruelty, surrendered to Shang Bibi.
translations.idiomatic: Jizang Fengzan, a general under the Tibetan warlord Lun Qiner, revolted against Qiner's cruelty and surrendered to Shang Bibi.
