sentences.zh: 恐熱發兵擊婢婢於鄯州，婢婢分兵為五道拒之。

translations.literal: Qiner raised troops and attacked Bibi at Shan Prefecture; Bibi divided her forces into five columns to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Qiner marched against Bibi at Shan Prefecture; Bibi split her army into five columns to meet him.

sentences.zh: 恐熱退保東谷，婢婢為木柵圍之，絕其水原。

translations.literal: Qiner retreated to hold Dong Valley; Bibi built wooden palisades to besiege him and cut off his water supply.
translations.idiomatic: Qiner fell back to Dong Valley; Bibi ringed him with wooden palisades and cut off his water.

sentences.zh: 恐熱將百餘騎突圍走保薄寒山，餘眾皆降於婢婢。

translations.literal: Qiner broke out with a little over a hundred horsemen and fled to hold Bo Han Mountain; the rest of his forces all surrendered to Bibi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiner broke out with barely a hundred riders and fled to Bo Han Mountain; the rest of his army surrendered to Bibi.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，王宰進攻澤州。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Wang Zai advanced to attack Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Wang Zai launched an assault on Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上好神仙，道士趙歸真得幸，諫官屢以為言。

translations.literal: The emperor favored immortals and Daoist lore; Zhao Guizhen won favor, and remonstrating officials repeatedly spoke against it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dabbled in immortality cults, and the Daoist Zhao Guizhen won his favor. Censorial officials remonstrated again and again.

sentences.zh: 丙子，李德裕亦諫曰：「歸真，敬宗朝罪人，不宜親近！」

translations.literal: On bingzi, Li Deyu also remonstrated: "Guizhen is a criminal from Emperor Jingzong's reign and should not be kept close!"
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Li Deyu remonstrated as well: "Guizhen is a convicted criminal from Jingzong's reign and should not be kept near the throne!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕宮中無事時與之談道滌煩耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When I have nothing to do in the palace I talk Dao with him to wash away vexation, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When I have idle hours in the palace I talk Dao with him to clear my mind—that is all.

sentences.zh: 至於政事，朕必問卿等與次對官，雖百歸真不能惑也。」

translations.literal: As for state affairs, I always consult you and the duty officers; a hundred Guizhens could not sway me."
translations.idiomatic: On state affairs I always consult you and the duty officers. A hundred Zhao Guizhens could not sway me."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「小人見勢利所在，則奔趣之，如夜蛾之投燭。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Petty men see where profit and power lie and rush toward it, like moths at night flying into a candle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "Petty men chase wherever profit and power lead, like moths darting into a flame at night.

sentences.zh: 聞旬日以來，歸真之門，車馬輻湊，願陛下深戒之！」

translations.literal: For ten days now I have heard that Guizhen's gate is packed with carriages and horses. I beg Your Majesty to guard against this deeply!"
translations.idiomatic: For ten days now I have heard that carriages and horses crowd Guizhen's gate. I beg Your Majesty to take this warning to heart!"

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以左僕射王起同平章事，充山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Wang Qi, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Co-Equal to the Department of State Affairs and Military Commissioner of the Western Mountain-North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wang Qi, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Grand Councilor and military commissioner of the Western Mountain-North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 起以文臣未嘗執政，直除使相，前無此比，固辭。

translations.literal: Qi, a civil official who had never held executive power, being directly appointed military commissioner and chief minister—there was no precedent—firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, a civil scholar who had never held executive office, was being made military commissioner and chief minister in one step—a thing without precedent—and he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「宰相無內外之異，朕有闕失，卿飛表以聞！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For a chief minister there is no distinction between inside and outside. If I have failings, send an urgent memorial to inform me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A chief minister knows no boundary between court and province. If I err, send an urgent memorial at once!"

sentences.zh: 李德裕以州縣佐官太冗，奏令吏部郎中柳仲郢裁減。

translations.literal: Li Deyu, because county and prefecture aide posts were too numerous, memorialized that Liu Zhongying, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, be ordered to trim them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu, finding county and prefecture aide posts far too numerous, memorialized that Liu Zhongying of the Ministry of Personnel be ordered to cut them back.

sentences.zh: 六月，仲郢奏減一千二百一十四員。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zhongying reported a reduction of 1,214 posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Zhongying reported a cut of 1,214 posts.

sentences.zh: 仲郢，公綽之子也。

translations.literal: Zhongying was the son of Gongchuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongying was the son of Liu Gongchuo.

sentences.zh: 宦官有發仇士良宿惡，於其家得兵仗數千。

translations.literal: Eunuchs exposed Qiu Shiliang's long-standing evils, and at his home found several thousand weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs exposed Qiu Shiliang's old crimes and found several thousand weapons in his house.

sentences.zh: 詔削其官爵，籍沒家貲。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his ranks and titles and confiscated his household property.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped him of rank and title and confiscated his estate.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛卯，上與李德裕議以王逢將兵屯翼城，上曰：「聞逢用法太嚴，有諸？」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, the emperor discussed with Li Deyu Wang Feng leading troops to encamp at Yicheng. The emperor said: "I hear Feng's enforcement of law is too harsh—is it so?"
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, the emperor discussed with Li Deyu Wang Feng's posting at Yicheng. He asked, "I hear Feng enforces discipline too harshly—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣亦嘗以此詰之，逢言：『前有白刃，法不嚴，其誰肯進？』

translations.literal: He replied: "I too once questioned him about this. Feng said: 'With naked blades ahead, if the law is not strict, who would dare advance?'
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu replied, "I questioned him myself. Feng said, 'With naked blades in front of us, if discipline is lax, who will dare advance?'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「言亦有理，卿更召而戒之！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "There is reason in that. Summon him again and admonish him!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "There is sense in that. Summon him again and counsel restraint!"

sentences.zh: 德裕因言劉稹不可赦。

translations.literal: Deyu then said Liu Zhen could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu then said Liu Zhen must not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「固然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Certainly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Of course."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「昔李懷光未平，京師蝗旱，米斗千錢，太倉米供天子及六宮無數旬之儲。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "In the past, before Li Huai'guang was pacified, the capital suffered locusts and drought; rice was a thousand cash per dou; the Grand Storehouse could not supply the emperor and the Six Palaces for many tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "Before Li Huai'guang was crushed, locusts and drought struck the capital. Rice cost a thousand cash per dou, and the Grand Storehouse could not feed the emperor and the inner palaces for many weeks.

sentences.zh: 德宗集百官，遣中使馬欽緒詢之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong assembled the officials and sent the palace attendant Ma Qinxu to inquire of them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong gathered the officials and sent the palace envoy Ma Qinxu to ask their counsel.

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍李泌取桐葉摶破，以授欽緒獻之。

translations.literal: Li Bi, Left Regular Palace Attendant, took a paulownia leaf, tore it apart, and handed it to Qinxu to present.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, Left Regular Palace Attendant, tore a paulownia leaf in two and gave the pieces to Qinxu to present.

sentences.zh: 德宗召問其故，對曰：『陛下與懷光君臣之分，如此葉不可復合矣！』

translations.literal: Dezong summoned him and asked the reason. He replied: "The relationship between Your Majesty and Huai'guang as sovereign and subject is like this leaf—it cannot be joined again!"
translations.idiomatic: Dezong summoned him and asked why. Li Bi answered, "The bond between Your Majesty and Huai'guang as sovereign and subject is like this leaf—it can never be made whole again!"

sentences.zh: 由是德宗意定。

translations.literal: From this Dezong's mind was settled.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment Dezong's resolve was firm.

sentences.zh: 既破懷光，遂用為相，獨任數年。」

translations.literal: After Huai'guang was defeated, he was made chief minister and entrusted alone for several years."
translations.idiomatic: After Huai'guang fell, Li Bi was made chief minister and held sole trust for years."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「亦大是奇士！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He was truly a remarkable man!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He was a remarkable man indeed!"

sentences.zh: 上聞揚州倡女善為酒令，敕淮南監軍選十七人獻之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that singing girls in Yang Prefecture were skilled at drinking games and ordered the Huainan army supervisor to select seventeen and present them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard that courtesans in Yangzhou were skilled at drinking games and ordered the Huainan army supervisor to select seventeen and send them to court.

sentences.zh: 監軍請節度使杜悰同選，且欲更擇良家美女，教而獻之。

translations.literal: The supervisor asked Military Commissioner Du Cong to join the selection and wished further to choose fine women from respectable families, train them, and present them.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor asked Military Commissioner Du Cong to help choose them and proposed selecting respectable beauties as well, training them, and presenting those too.

sentences.zh: 悰曰：「監軍自受敕，悰不敢預聞！」

translations.literal: Cong said: "The supervisor received the edict himself—I dare not involve myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong said, "The supervisor received the edict on his own authority—I dare not take part!"

sentences.zh: 監軍再三請之，不從。

translations.literal: The supervisor repeatedly pressed him; he refused.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor pressed him again and again; Du Cong refused.

sentences.zh: 監軍怒，具表其狀，上覽表默然。

translations.literal: The supervisor grew angry and submitted a full report. The emperor read it in silence.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor grew angry and submitted a full report. The emperor read it and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 左右請並敕節度使同選，上曰：「敕籓方選倡女入宮，豈聖天子所為！

translations.literal: Those around him asked that the military commissioner also be ordered to select. The emperor said: "Ordering a frontier region to select singing girls for the palace—how is that the act of a sage Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Those around him suggested ordering the military commissioner to join the selection. The emperor said, "Ordering a frontier province to send courtesans to the palace—is that what a sage Son of Heaven does!

sentences.zh: 杜悰不徇監軍意，得大臣體，真宰相才也。

translations.literal: Du Cong did not follow the army supervisor's wish and upheld the bearing of a great minister. He truly has the talent of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong refused to bend to the army supervisor and showed the bearing of a true minister. He has the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 朕甚愧之！」

translations.literal: I am deeply ashamed of this!"
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply ashamed!"

sentences.zh: 遽敕監軍勿復選。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the army supervisor not to select any more.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the army supervisor to stop the selection.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以悰同平章事，兼度支、鹽鐵轉過使。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Cong was made Co-Equal to the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Commissioner for Revenue, Salt Iron, and Transport.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen, Du Cong was made Grand Councilor and concurrently Commissioner for Revenue, Salt Iron, and Transport.

sentences.zh: 及悰中謝，上勞之曰：「卿不從監軍之言，朕知卿有致君之心，今相卿，如得一魏徵矣！」

translations.literal: When Cong came to express thanks at court, the emperor comforted him, saying: "You did not follow the supervisor's words; I know you have the heart to serve your ruler well. Now that I have made you chief minister, it is like gaining a Wei Zheng!"
translations.idiomatic: When Du Cong came to court to express thanks, the emperor praised him, saying, "You refused the supervisor's request—I know you have the heart to serve your ruler. Making you chief minister now is like gaining a Wei Zheng!"
